title: 第四章　一个政权的诞生：战时共产主义，1918—1921
originalTitle: 4 A REGIME IS BORN War Communism, 1918-1921

德瓦诺夫想出一项发明：把阳光转化为电。为此，戈普纳把切文古尔所有镜子从镜框中取出，还收集了每一小块厚玻璃。德瓦诺夫和戈普纳用这些材料制作了复杂的棱镜和反射器，使阳光穿过它们时发生转化，到装置末端变成电流。装置已经完成两天了，却仍然没有电出现。大家都来看德瓦诺夫的光机，虽然它不运转，大家还是认定它是需要的：这台机器在政治上是正确的、必要的，因为它是两位可靠同志用体力劳动设想并制造出来的。

zh: 是战争使布尔什维克夺取政权成为可能；又是战争规定了新苏维埃秩序的基本制度得以建立的条件。党的“无产阶级专政”就这样作为战时共产主义诞生于世。而这头粗暴的野兽将是军事共产主义与战斗性共产主义的混合体，两个组成部分彼此滋养，同时又相互强化。
en: It was war that had made possible the Bolshevik seizure of power; and it was war that would set the parameters within which the basic institutions of the new Soviet order would be built. The Party’s “dictatorship of the proletariat” thus was born into the world as War Communism. And this rough beast would be a hybrid of military communism and militant communism, in which each component fed on, and at the same time reinforced, the other.

zh: 1917年10月，布尔什维克成功占据了权力机关的实际所在地，但他们还远未处于真正行使权力的位置。接管一个大国的神经中枢固然不是小事，但这种壮举在欧洲历史上并非没有先例，1871年的公社社员几乎也做到了同样的事。对布尔什维克胆识的真正考验，将是他们巩固权力、建立一种运转的新秩序的能力；而他们在1918年至1921年——内战和战时共产主义年代——以一场空前的革命活力迸发通过了这场考验。
en: In October 1917 the Bolsheviks had succeeded in occupying the physical seats of power, but they were hardly in a position to actually wield power. Though it was no small feat to take over the nerve centers of a major state, such an exploit was not without precedent in European history, and the Communards of 1871 had done almost as much. The real test of the Bolshevik’s mettle would be their ability to consolidate power and to build a functioning new order; and they met this test in an unprecedented outburst of revolutionary vigor between 1918 and 1921, the years of the Civil War and War Communism.

zh: 这些年是共产主义作为一种现实存在制度的奠基年代，是苏维埃主义母体定型、并将在此后四分之三个世纪中延续下去的时期。事实上，这一进程最具“创造性”的阶段是1918年，所有使苏维埃制度成为可能的根本措施都在这一年采取。俄国革命真正决定性的年份是1918年，而不是1917年。正是在这一年，新型政党通过创造一个全新类型的社会，展示了它究竟有多新。
en: These years were the founding years of Communism as a really-existing system, the time when the matrix of Sovietism as it would endure for the next three-quarters of a century was set. Indeed, the most “creative” stage of this process was the year 1918, during which all the essential measures were taken that made the Soviet system possible. It is 1918, not 1917, that is the truly decisive year of the Russian Revolution. This is the year in which the Party of a new type showed just how new it was by creating an entire society of a new type.

zh: 党是通过对一连串危机的果敢回应来创造这个独特社会的，而那些危机本会压垮任何较弱形式的政治组织。然而这些回应绝不是乍看之下那种随意的临时应付；相反，它们揭示出一种政治意志的模式，其方向是让一切社会“自发性”服从于党的“自觉性”。
en: The Party created this unique society by its daring responses to a succession of crises that would have overwhelmed any lesser form of political organization. Yet these responses are by no means the haphazard improvisations they may seem to be at first glance; rather, they reveal a pattern of political will directed towards the subordination of all social “spontaneity” to Party “consciousness.”

zh: 坠入混乱
en: THE DESCENT INTO CHAOS

zh: 布尔什维克领导层在十月的预期是，俄国革命将引发一场革命，为全欧洲的资本主义敲响丧钟。实现这一点的机制，是各交战国士兵之间的友好交往：这场响应10月26日苏维埃和平法令的运动，将使苏维埃在各地掌权。十月之后的头几个月，列宁、托洛茨基以及布尔什维克和左派社会革命党领导层中的其他人都坚信，帝国主义战争这种革命性的结束近在眼前。这种信念在党内的下层和工人阶级中传播到何种程度，难以判断；但可以合理猜测，尽管有反帝国主义观点的不懈宣传，大多数俄国人只是简单地、非理论地反对战争，不论其政治后果如何。然而，对于当时俄国左派中作决策的人来说，十月只有作为引爆器才有意义，其本身并不是目的。
en: The expectation of the Bolshevik leadership in October was that the Russian Revolution would trigger a revolution that would sound the death knell for capitalism across Europe. The mechanism by which this would be achieved was fraternization among the various belligerent armies: This movement, a response to the Soviet Peace Decree of October 26, would bring soviets to power everywhere. In the first months after October, Lenin, Trotsky, and others in the Bolshevik and the Left SR (Socialist Revolutionary) leaderships all firmly believed that such a revolutionary end to the imperialist war was imminent. How far down in Party ranks and in the working class this belief extended is difficult to say; but it is a fair guess that, despite relentless propaganda for the anti-imperialist view, most Russians were simply, and untheoretically, against the war regardless of the political consequences. For the people making the decisions on the Left in Russia at the time, however, October made sense only as a detonator, not as an end in itself.

zh: 这种信念的一个推论是：一旦资本主义崩溃，社会主义就会自动出现，而且或多或少是完整成形的，因为据称它已经存在于“资产阶级社会的子宫中”，如马克思所说。列宁更新了马克思的这一命题，以考虑“金融资本”和“帝国主义”时代的创新。在他看来，进行现代战争所需的总体动员，代表了经济生活的理性组织，而这就是社会主义的本质；因此，只要结束战争，从而推翻资本主义，社会主义就几乎会自行到来。由于这个原因，列宁对埃里希·冯·鲁登道夫将军及其经济计划者瓦尔特·拉特瑙的政策评价极高，他们自己把这些政策称为

，即战争社会主义。列宁还在其中加入了他对泰勒制——一种“科学的”美国式劳动合理组织方法——的信念。因此，真正的社会主义将由无产阶级政权实施类似政策而产生。而这一切都会相当快地到来，经过一个列宁有时称为“国家资本主义”的中间阶段，这基本上是战争社会主义的另一个名称。因此，十月之后布尔什维克的政策，是通过对现有资本主义工业体系实行国家控制，开始在俄国向社会主义前进，同时等待欧洲、尤其是德国的革命，使完整社会主义在全欧洲成为可能。
en: A corollary to this belief was that once capitalism had collapsed, socialism would automatically appear, more or less full-blown, because it was allegedly already present “in the womb of bourgeois society,” as Marx put it. Lenin had updated this proposition of Marx to take account of the innovations of the age of “finance capital” and “imperialism.” In his view, the total mobilization required to wage modern war represented that rational organization of economic life that was the essence of socialism; it would therefore be enough to end the war, thereby overthrowing capitalism, and socialism would practically be there. For this reason, Lenin had the highest regard for the policies of General Erich von Ludendorff and his economic planner Walter Rathenau, policies that they themselves called

, or War Socialism. And to these Lenin added his belief in the “scientific” American method of Taylorism for the rational organization of work. Real socialism, therefore, would result from similar policies implemented by proletarian power. And all this would come about fairly soon, after an intermediate stage that Lenin sometimes called “state capitalism,” which is essentially another term for War Socialism. The Bolshevik policy after October, therefore, was to begin the advance toward socialism in Russia by imposing state control on the existing capitalist industrial system while awaiting the European, especially the German, revolution that would make full socialism possible across the continent.

zh: 但随着月份拖入1918年，帝国主义战争并没有以革命告终。很快就显而易见，俄国通过国家资本主义向社会主义的初步推进，将在可预见的未来构成布尔什维克全部经济政策。换句话说，无论从资本主义链条最薄弱环节即俄国环节断裂之后会随之而来什么样的更完整社会主义，都必须由苏维埃政权来设计，得不到先进西方的任何投入。于是，随着事态进入夏天，设计社会主义的努力压倒了此前等待社会主义的政策，国家资本主义让位于战时共产主义。简言之，当历史逻辑没有自动产生社会主义时，党就必须强行推动历史进程；也就是说，社会主义必须被“建设”出来，正如苏联人后来所说。而正是建设社会主义的渴望，提供了支配布尔什维克1918年一切看似临时应付之举的模式或逻辑。
en: But as the months dragged on into 1918. the imperialist war did not end in revolution. It soon became apparent that Russia’s tentative advance towards socialism through state capitalism would be the whole of the Bolsheviks’ economic policy for the foreseeable future. In other words, whatever fuller socialism would follow from breaking the capitalist chain at its weakest, Russian link would have to be engineered by Soviet power without any input from the advanced West. So, as events moved on into the summer, the effort to engineer socialism eclipsed the previous policy of waiting for it, and state capitalism gave way to War Communism. In short, when the logic of history did not produce socialism automatically, the hand of history had to be forced by the Party; that is, socialism would have to be “built,” as the Soviets would later say. And it is the aspiration to build socialism that furnished the pattern, or the logic, that governed all of the Bolsheviks’ seeming improvisations in 1918.

zh: 这一点值得强调，因为布尔什维克在整个内战时期的政策常常被贬为半偶然的，是对列宁主义原初路线的偏离——原初路线是等待客观条件充分成熟，使真正的社会主义成为可能。而这种过早的、强行军式地进入新社会，则被解释为内战中求生存的残酷需要。结果，这一时期在列宁主义史学中显得像一个被忽视的穷亲戚，是记述创始人业绩时应当尽快翻过去的尴尬一页。然而这种态度是严重错误，因为战时共产主义对整个苏维埃经验具有奠基意义。战时共产主义不是偏离，而是第一次向布尔什维克揭示他们实际上是谁的关键篇章。
en: This point bears emphasizing because the Bolsheviks’ policies throughout the Civil War are too often dismissed as quasi-accidental, an aberration from the original Leninist course of waiting for objective circumstances to mature sufficiently for genuine socialism to become possible. And this premature, forced march into the New Society is explained by the cruel exigencies of the struggle for survival in the Civil War. In consequence, this period appears as a neglected poor relation in the historiography of Leninism, an embarrassment to be gotten over as rapidly as possible in chronicling the work of the Founder. This attitude, however, is a grave error, for War Communism was seminal to the whole Soviet experience. War Communism was no aberration, but the crucial episode that first revealed to the Bolsheviks who they in fact were.

zh: 这场炮火下的自我发现过程，始于十月之后不久，一直持续到次年秋天。它由一连串危机推动，这些危机表明，从战争到经济的一切困扰临时政府的问题都没有消失，反而在苏维埃政权自身的瓦解性冲击下变得更糟。然而新政府不同于其前任，并没有在压力下崩溃；相反，灾难刺激它采取越来越大胆、越来越激烈的行动。
en: This process of self-discovery under fire began in the immediate aftermath of October and lasted until the autumn of the following year. It was propelled by a succession of crises that showed that all of the problems—from the war to the economy—that had plagued the Provisional Government had not disappeared but had grown worse under the disintegrative impact of Soviet power itself. Yet the new government, unlike its predecessor, did not collapse under the strain; rather, catastrophe galvanized it into ever bolder and more drastic action.

zh: 布尔什维克必须面对的第一个问题是国家权力，他们以警察措施消灭一切竞争性权力中心，勉强解决了这个问题。

列宁最早的行动之一，是在1917年12月7日设立“全俄肃清反革命及怠工非常委员会”，通称契卡，由一位投身布尔什维主义的波兰贵族费利克斯·捷尔任斯基领导。这个无产阶级专政的臂膀被视为必要，以剥夺以前的剥削阶级——资产阶级和贵族——并镇压其政治活动。然而很快，“投机”和“囤积”这类“经济犯罪”也归入契卡的管辖范围。换句话说，列宁从一开始就在准备对苏维埃政权的一切阶级敌人发动内战。虽然这场战争的最初枪声实际上是由白卫志愿军1917年12月在顿河哥萨克地区打响的，但正是布尔什维克对权力垄断的僭取，使反对力量除了武装抵抗别无选择。
en: The first problem the Bolsheviks had to face was that of state power, and this they solved, after a fashion, by eliminating all rival loci of power through police measures.

Among Lenin’s very first acts, on December 7, 1917, was to establish the Extraordinary Commission for the Struggle against Counterrevolution and Sabotage, commonly known as the Cheka, under the leadership of a Polish nobleman rallied to Bolshevism, Felix Dzerzhinskii. This arm of the proletarian dictatorship was deemed necessary to dispossess the former exploiting classes—the bourgeoisie and the gentry—and to suppress their political activities. Very soon, however, such “economic crimes” as “speculation” and “hoarding” came under the Cheka’s jurisdiction. In other words, Lenin from the beginning was preparing to wage civil war against all the class enemies of Soviet power. Although the first shots in this war were actually fired by the White Volunteer Army in the region of the Don Cossacks in December, it was the Bolsheviks’ presumption to exercise a monopoly of power that left opposition forces no recourse but armed resistance.

zh: 但这场战争中的第一次重大冲突，发生在布尔什维克与其他所有政党之间。1917年底，终于举行了基于普选权的立宪会议选举。选举结果与其说是宪政民主的胜利，不如说是社会革命的胜利；唯一以宪政民主为第一原则的政党立宪民主党人，只获得4.7%的选票。但选举也不是布尔什维克的胜利；他们在选票和席位上都只得到24%。明显的领先者是变化多端的社会革命党，得票约40%，这使主流派即“右派”社会革命党人获得代表总数的54%，左派社会革命党人获得5.5%（社会革命党的单一名单是在两派分裂之前拟定的）。孟什维克和立宪民主党人各得约2%的席位。
en: But the first major clash in the war was between the Bolsheviks and all the other political parties. Elections for the Constituent Assembly, on the basis of universal suffrage, at last took place at the end of 1917. The results were more a victory for social revolution than for constitutional democracy; the only party for whom the latter system was the first principle, the Kadets, received only 4.7 percent of the vote. But the elections were not a victory for the Bolsheviks, either; they received 24 percent of both votes and seats. The clear leader was the protean SR Party with about 40 percent of the vote, and this yielded the mainstream, or “Right,” SRs 54 percent of the total delegates and the Left SRs 5.5 percent (the single SR list had been drawn up before the two groups split). The Mensheviks and Kadets had about 2 percent of the seats each.

zh: 因此，尽管约85%的席位归于某种色彩的社会主义者，立宪会议仍然不是一个会听命于布尔什维克、或承认其“苏维埃”政府的机构。列宁通过如下论证解决了这个问题：第一，主流社会革命党代表团并不代表基层，他声称基层在单一选举名单拟定之后已转向他那种左派。更重要的论证是目的论的：只有劳动阶级的“苏维埃”民主，才“高于”一人一票的“资产阶级”民主。于是，在选举过程中，他取缔了“资产阶级”立宪民主党人。当立宪会议于1918年1月6日开会时，他在波罗的海舰队水兵的帮助下驱散了它；那些水兵对会议主席、社会革命党人维克托·切尔诺夫说“卫队累了”，叫他滚蛋。
en: Thus, although some 85 percent of the seats went to socialists of one or another stripe, the Assembly was still not a body that would do the Bolsheviks’ bidding or recognize their “Soviet” government. Lenin solved this problem by arguing, first, that the mainstream SR delegation was not representative of the base, which he held had moved to his kind of Left after the single electoral list had been drawn up. A more important argument was the teleological one that the “soviet” democracy of the toiling classes alone was “higher” than the “bourgeois” democracy of one man, one vote. Thus in the course of the elections he had outlawed the “bourgeois” Kadets. And when the Assembly met on January 6, 1918, he dispersed it with the help of sailors from the Baltic Fleet who, with the words “the guard is tired,” told its chairman, the SR Victor Chernov, to decamp.

zh: 驱散立宪会议通常被指控为布尔什维克对民主犯下的最高罪行，与十月政变同属一类。这完全属实。但人们不常指出的是，从现实角度看，这个机构几乎不可能在当时日益加剧的混乱中实行治理。正如托洛茨基略带夸张地说，政治上立宪会议不过是临时政府投向未来的苍白影子。因为立宪会议由那些在1917年掌权时未能掌控局势的同一批政党主导；它没有武装力量，没有行政机构，甚至在苏维埃中也没有；它也没有纲领：它通过的两项决议只是对布尔什维克和平法令和土地法令的认可。最后，它没有准备好为其治理权而战的选民。农民一旦得到土地，就对政治失去兴趣；而工人暂时仍以为苏维埃真的是他们的。因此，立宪会议的消亡没有引起任何真正的抵抗，甚至没有愤怒。至于非资产阶级政党——多数派社会革命党人和孟什维克——它们在法律形式上仍然合法，但随着内战推进，实际上越来越受到骚扰。
en: The dispersal of the Constituent Assembly is usually alleged to be the Bolsheviks’ supreme crime, on a footing with the October coup, against democracy. And this is quite true. But it is not often enough noted that, realistically, this body could hardly have governed amidst the mounting disorder of the time. As Trotsky put it, with only slight exaggeration, politically the Assembly was nothing more than the pale shadow that the Provisional Government had cast before itself into the future. For the Assembly was dominated by the same parties that had been unable to master the situation when they were in power in 1917; it had no armed forces and no administrative apparatus, not even in the soviets. Nor did it have a program: the only two resolutions it adopted were simply endorsements of the Bolsheviks’ decrees on peace and land. Finally, it had no constituency prepared to fight for its right to govern. Once the peasants had the land, they lost interest in politics; and the workers, for the time being, still thought that the soviets were really theirs. So no real resistance, or even outrage, answered the Assembly’s demise. As for the nonbourgeois parties—the majority SRs and the Mensheviks—they continued to be technically legal, but in practice they were increasingly harassed as the Civil War progressed.

zh: 不久，列宁就抛弃了他唯一的社会主义盟友——左派社会革命党人。1918年1月，预见到与立宪会议的麻烦，并在中央委员会中较胆怯成员的催促下，列宁接受了与四名左派社会革命党部长组成的联合政府。但他们于三月辞职，以抗议他在布列斯特-立托夫斯克与德国人签订和约。从那时起直到1991年苏维埃国家灭亡，政府事务严格属于一党。很难相信，这种一党制的迅速出现，是一场尚未开始的内战强加给列宁和托洛茨基的。一党秩序从一开始就隐含在十月颠覆之中，布尔什维克单方面夺权只是被一层苏维埃门面勉强遮掩。
en: Soon Lenin dispatched his only socialist allies, the Left SRs. In January 1918, in anticipation of trouble with the Assembly and pressed by the more timorous members of his Central Committee, Lenin had accepted a coalition government with four Left SR ministers. But they resigned in March in protest against his peace with the Germans at Brest-Litovsk. From then until the demise of the Soviet state in 1991, government was strictly a one-party affair. It is difficult to believe that this swift emergence of a one-party regime was forced on Lenin and Trotsky by a civil war that had not yet begun. A one-party order was implicit from the beginning in the October overturn, in which the unilateral Bolshevik seizure of power was barely camouflaged by a facade of soviets.

children: 〔译注〕关于联合政府的开始时间，有研究将布尔什维克与左派社会革命党人在人民委员会的合作期列为1917年12月至1918年3月。
〔译注〕关于联合政府的开始时间，有研究将布尔什维克与左派社会革命党人在人民委员会的合作期列为1917年12月至1918年3月。

zh: 不过，党并不直接治理。它通过一个表面上正常的国家机器进行统治，这个机器名为“苏维埃”，并通过贴着民粹主义标签“人民委员部”的部委行使权力。这种安排被不同地称为党国或双重国家，是布尔什维克在政治上的伟大创新。在这个双重国家中，国家的真正权力掌握在党手中；党是一个自我任命、完全通过内部吸纳招募的组织，因此实际上是一个秘密会社，或所谓“掌权中的阴谋集团”，在幕后通过一个理论上以人民为依托的正式国家机器进行统治。在这种二分法中，党就是后来人们所说的“权力”，而苏维埃行政网络则是它的“机关”。
en: Still, the Party did not govern directly. Rather, it ruled through an ostensibly normal state apparatus that bore the name “Soviet” and exercised its power through ministries given the populist label “People’s Commissariats.” This arrangement, which has been variously called the Party-state or the dual state, is the great Bolshevik innovation in politics. In this dual state, real power in the country was held by the Party, a self-appointed organization recruited entirely by cooptation; it was thus in effect a secret society, or what has been called a “conspiracy in power,” which ruled behind the scenes through a formal state apparatus theoretically resting on the people. In this dichotomy the Party was “the power,” as people later said, and the Soviet administrative network was its “apparat.”

zh: 契卡和党国框架都是在十月之后头三个月内建立的，那时对布尔什维克权力的任何严重挑战尚未出现（南方出现的微小白色运动当时还不构成威胁）。然而这两个制度仍处于胚胎状态。在接下来的八个月里，在一连串灾难的冲击下，它们将发育完全；到八月，这些灾难似乎就要把布尔什维克政权整个扫除。
en: Both the Cheka and the framework of the Party-state were created during the first three months after October, before any serious challenge to Bolshevik power had emerged (the miniscule White movement that had appeared in the south was as yet no threat). These two institutions, however, were still embryonic. In the next eight months they were to attain their full stature under the impact of a cascade of calamities that by August seemed about to sweep the Bolshevik regime away entirely.

zh: 这些危机中的第一个，由灾难性的布列斯特和约引起。1917年11月的停战，导致同盟国与苏维埃政府于十二月在该城进行和平谈判。布尔什维克的目的当然不是与谈判对手缔结和平；而是把谈判当作宣传讲坛，反对帝国主义战争，主张“没有兼并和赔款的民主和平”。他们希望借此促成两军士兵之间的友好交往，并通过这种交往把帝国主义战争转变为一场导致社会主义革命的国际阶级战争。简言之，他们把在国内使他们掌权的最大化策略投射到了国际舞台。
en: The first of these crises was occasioned by the disastrous peace of Brest-Litovsk. An armistice in November 1917 led to peace negotiations in that city between the Central Powers and the Soviet government in December. The purpose of the Bolsheviks, of course, was not to negotiate a peace with their interlocutors; it was to use the negotiations as a propaganda platform against the imperialist war and for “a democratic peace without annexations or indemnities.” Thereby, they hoped to produce fraternization between the troops of the two armies, and through this to transform the imperialist war into an international class war leading to socialist revolution. In short, they were projecting into the international arena the maximalist tactics that had brought them power at home.,

zh: 但这项事业由托洛茨基以他十月主持彼得格勒苏维埃时同样的革命热情来推进，却在布列斯特-立托夫斯克以惨败告终。同盟国士兵没有被说服；他们的指挥官很快对布尔什维克的表演失去耐心；二月，他们的军队再次开始向俄国推进。但此时俄国已没有军队可以抵抗。首都匆忙从彼得格勒迁往莫斯科，以远离前线。列宁力主采取现实路线，接受一项被强加的“帝国主义”和约，以挽救苏维埃政权。托洛茨基、布哈林等人则浪漫地主张某种版本的“革命战争”——即游击战争——以阻止德军推进，并把革命向西传播。列宁在党内和苏维埃代表大会上仅以最微弱的多数获胜。但国家付出的代价是巨大的：波罗的海诸省、乌克兰和俄国南部直到高加索，都落入德国控制。这些领土占旧帝国欧洲部分的整整三分之一，占帝国工业能力和粮食生产的近一半。但这就是在一场失败的战争中单独媾和的代价。正是因为可能面临类似条件，临时政府才从不敢单方面退出那场正在摧毁它的战争。
en: But this enterprise, conducted by Trotsky with the same revolutionary gusto with which he had presided over the Petrograd Soviet in October, led to fiasco at Brest-Litovsk. The soldiers of the Central Powers were not swayed; their commanders soon lost patience with Bolshevik grandstanding; and in February their armies again began to advance into Russia. But by this time Russia no longer had an army with which to resist them. The capital was hastily moved from Petrograd to Moscow so as to be farther from the front. Lenin urged the realistic course of accepting a dictated, “imperialist” peace in order to save the Soviet regime. Trotsky, Bukharin, and others romantically advocated one version or another of “revolutionary”—that is, guerrilla—war to stop the German advance and spread the Revolution westward. Lenin carried the day in the Party and in the Soviet Congress by only the narrowest of margins. But the cost to the country was enormous: The Baltic provinces, Ukraine, and southern Russia on into the Caucasus passed under German control. These territories represented a third of the European portion of the old Empire and almost half of the Empire’s industrial capacity and food production. But such is the price of a separate peace in a losing war. It was because of the likelihood of similar terms that the Provisional Government had never dared to unilaterally leave the war that was destroying it.

zh: 列宁的理由当然是：既然世界革命仍迫在眉睫，布列斯特的让步很快就会作废；与此同时，首要考虑是获得一个“喘息空间”，以便在社会主义权力唯一存在的地方巩固社会主义权力，也就是党的权力。列宁在这场生存危机中的“现实主义”受到许多历史学家的赞扬，包括那些对苏维埃政权并无好感的人。但他在这件事和其他事情上的现实主义很容易被夸大：它关乎策略，而非战略，因为他的现实主义始终以世界革命这一狂热的意识形态前提为根据——正如他在十月时的现实主义一样。尽管如此，凭借布列斯特和约带来的喘息空间，他作为革命领袖取得了第二次伟大胜利，因为这场新的赌博最终随着年底同盟国的崩溃而得到了回报。
en: Lenin’s rationale, of course, was that since world revolution was still imminent, the concessions of Brest-Litovsk would soon be wiped out; in the meantime, the overriding consideration was to obtain a “breathing space” to consolidate socialist power, which was also the Party’s power, in the only place it existed. Lenin’s “realism” in this crisis of survival has been much praised by historians, including those unsympathetic to the Soviet regime. Yet his realism in this and other matters can be exaggerated: It concerned tactics, not strategy, for his realism was always predicated on the wild ideological premises of world revolution—as had been the case with his realism in October. Nonetheless, with his Brest-Litovsk breathing space, he scored his second great coup as a revolutionary leader, for eventually this new gamble did pay off with the collapse of the Central Powers at the end of the year.

zh: 然而短期内，布列斯特-立托夫斯克给苏维埃政权制造了新的生死攸关问题。签署“帝国主义”和约的决定，分裂了十月的左翼联盟。首先，布尔什维克内部出现暂时分裂，尼古拉·布哈林和一批左派共产主义者脱离党的队列，继续鼓动革命战争。更严重的是，左派社会革命党人退出了正月组成的联合政府，转入积极反对，以推翻布列斯特和约。很快，布尔什维克对农民的压力又给了他们一个更有力的反对理由。
en: In the short term, however, Brest-Litovsk created new life-threatening problems for the Soviet regime. The decision to sign an “imperialist” peace split the Left coalition of October. There was, first, a temporary schism among the Bolsheviks when Nikolai Bukharin and a group of Left Communists broke Party ranks to continue agitating for revolutionary war. More serious still, the Left SRs left the coalition formed in January and went into active opposition to undo the Brest peace. Soon they were given a more potent reason for opposition because of Bolshevik pressure on the peasants.

zh: 这种压力采取的形式，是一项重大的布尔什维克农业新政策——“乡村中的阶级斗争”——下文将更详细讨论。此处只需指出，到四五月间，俄国中部地区——旧帝国仍处于布尔什维克控制的唯一部分——的经济开始瓦解。在经历了一个使彼得格勒和莫斯科人口减少约三分之一的漫长冬天之后，城市感受到饥饿。党试图通过在村庄中宣布“阶级斗争”来应对这个问题。这意味着煽动“贫农”——他们在村庄中相当于“无产阶级”——去榨取“小资产阶级富农”的“余粮”；这项政策在6月11日达到顶点，颁布法令组织“贫农委员会”。
尽管这项政策几乎没能收上粮食，它确实产生了政治效果：使农民疏远政权，并把左派社会革命党人变成武装反对派。
en: The form this pressure took was a momentous new Bolshevik agrarian policy—“class warfare in the village”—which will be discussed more fully below. At this point, suffice it to note that by April-May the economy of the central Russian regions—the only parts of the old Empire that remained under Bolshevik control-was beginning to come apart. Hunger was felt in the cities at the end of a long winter that had seen the populations of Petrograd and Moscow decline by about a third. The Party sought to meet this problem by proclaiming “class warfare” in the villages. This meant inciting the “poor peasants”—the functional equivalent in the villages of the “proletariat”—to extort the “surplus” grain of the “petty bourgeois kulaks”; this policy culminated on June 11 with a decree organizing “Committees of the Village Poor.”
Although this policy brought in almost no grain, it did have the political effect of alienating the peasants from the regime and turning the Left SRs into an armed opposition.

zh: 接着，在五月末六月初，看似最终的灾难降临了。约三万五千名捷克战俘曾被编入帝国军队对奥作战的支队，如今沿着从伏尔加河横跨西伯利亚直到符拉迪沃斯托克的线路分布。这些捷克部队正等待经海路绕行世界前往法国西线，但由于担心可能被布尔什维克解除武装，他们夺取了整条西伯利亚大铁路。
en: Then, in late May and early June, what seemed like the ultimate disaster struck. Some thirty-five thousand Czech prisoners of war who had been formed into detachments of the Imperial army to fight against Austria were now strung along a line running from the Volga across Siberia to Vladivostok. Awaiting evacuation around the world to the western front in France, but fearing that they might be disarmed by the Bolsheviks, the Czech troops seized the whole trans-Siberian railroad line.

zh: 苏维埃政权随即在铁路沿线各地崩溃。主流社会革命党人从阴影中重新出现，在伏尔加河畔的萨马拉召集了一个残缺的立宪会议。出现一个取代列宁政府的政府，如今成为现实的可能，而南方的小规模白卫运动也突然获得了真正的基础。与此同时，西方盟国对俄国在布列斯特的背弃极为愤怒，如今看到了重新开辟东线的可能。因此，盟国告诉捷克人留在原地，并开始亲自干预，反对红军。应当指出，正是这种军事考虑——而不是布尔什维克所声称的经济帝国主义——促成了盟国对革命的干预。
en: Soviet power immediately collapsed everywhere along the route. The mainstream SRs reemerged from the shadows and convened a rump Constituent Assembly in Samara on the Volga. An alternative government to that of Lenin now became a serious possibility, and the small White movement in the south suddenly acquired a genuine base. Meanwhile, the Western Allies, furious at Russia’s desertion at Brest-Litovsk, now saw the possibility of reopening an eastern front. The Allies therefore told the Czechs to stay put and began to intervene themselves against the Reds. It should be noted that it is this military consideration—not economic imperialism as the Bolsheviks claimed—that motivated the Allied intervention in the Revolution.

zh: 到六月，布尔什维克俄国已被压缩到大致相当于中世纪莫斯科大公国的区域。即便在这一区域内，布尔什维克的控制也不稳固。七月，左派社会革命党人试图在莫斯科发动起义，目的是把俄国拖入对德国的革命战争；鲍里斯·萨温科夫则在伏尔加河上游的雅罗斯拉夫尔发动起义。初生的白卫军也从乌拉尔向中伏尔加推进。接着在八月，一名左派社会革命党恐怖分子差点成功刺杀列宁。到夏末，看起来布尔什维克的冒险可能很快结束，整个插曲将作为第二个、更宏大的巴黎公社载入史册——一场光荣的失败，只作为未来社会主义革命的灯塔而长存。
en: By June Bolshevik Russia had been reduced to roughly the area of the medieval Grand Principality of Moscow. Even within this area the Bolsheviks’ control was unsteady. In July the Left SRs attempted a revolt in Moscow with the aim of drawing Russia into revolutionary war with Germany, and Boris Savinkov staged an uprising in laroslavl on the upper Volga. Rudimentary White armies were also advancing from the Urals to the middle Volga. Then, in August, a Left SR terrorist nearly succeeded in killing Lenin. By the summer’s end it looked as if the Bolshevik adventure might soon be over and the whole episode would enter history as a second, grander Paris Commune, a glorious failure that would live only as a beacon for future socialist revolutions.

zh: 党反击
en: THE PARTY STRIKES BACK

zh: 正是为了回应这一连串危机，十月产生的胚胎式党国才发育完全。布尔什维克的反攻同时在三条主要战线上展开。第一，是对所有其他政党进行阶级战争的政治—行政战线。第二，是对白卫军作战的内战军事战线。最后，是狭义战时共产主义的经济战线，即建设社会主义秩序。
en: It was in response to this succession of crises that the embryonic Party-state which had emerged from October grew to full stature. The Bolshevik counteroffensive developed simultaneously on three main fronts. First, there was the political-administrative front of class war against all other parties. Second, there was the military front of the Civil War against the Whites. And finally, there was the economic front of War Communism narrowly defined, that is, the building of a socialist order.

zh: 从1918年春天开始，契卡被赋予新的任务，并大力执行，不仅用于打击白卫军，也用于击退非布尔什维克社会主义力量的复苏。随着局势在春天恶化，党的工人“基础”开始瓦解，孟什维克和社会革命党人再次在苏维埃中赢得多数；作为回应，这些机构干脆被契卡清洗掉“小资产阶级”分子，由可靠的布尔什维克取而代之。
随着七月、八月左派社会革命党人起义和白卫军向俄国中部推进使布尔什维克权力的危险加剧，无处不在的苏维埃网络被完全置于党之下；从那时起，苏维埃纯粹是形式上的机构。
en: Beginning in the spring of 1918, the Cheka was put to vigorous new uses, not only to combat the Whites, but to roll back a resurgence of non-Bolshevik socialist strength. As the situation deteriorated during the spring, the Party’s worker “base” began to crumble, and Mensheviks and SRs once again won majorities in the soviets; in answer, those bodies were simply purged of the “petty bourgeois” elements by the Cheka, and reliable Bolsheviks were appointed in their place.

And as the danger to Bolshevik power increased in July and August with the Left SR revolt and the White advance on central Russia, the omnipresent network of soviets was wholly subordinated to the Party; from that time on, the soviets were purely formal institutions.

zh: 于是到夏末，列宁在《国家与革命》中颂扬、并在1917年事实上初具轮廓的公社国家，已完全让位于党国。
随后，在八月刺杀列宁的企图之后，政权正式宣布红色恐怖政策，由契卡对人民、革命和党的一切敌人实施。于是，“无产阶级专政”获得了它革命后的完整含义，即列宁喜欢说的“不受任何法律限制的无限权力”。
en: Thus by the end of the summer the commune state, celebrated by Lenin in
and adumbrated in fact in 1917, had fully given way to the Party-state.

Then, after the August attempt on Lenin’s life, the regime officially proclaimed a policy of Red Terror, which would be directed by the Cheka against all enemies of the people, of the Revolution, and of the Party. And so the “dictatorship of the proletariat” came to acquire its full, postrevolutionary meaning of an “unlimited power above all law,” as Lenin liked to put the matter.

zh: 对不断升级的灾难的第二种回应，即军事回应，紧接布列斯特和约之后到来。它包括用基于征兵、纪律和自上而下指挥链等常规公式的红军，取代1917年建立的赤卫队民兵。
关键措施——征兵——于4月22日实行，托洛茨基则把才能从外交转向战争，出任这个新革命机构的总司令。因为红军尽管恢复了等级制和纪律，仍然是一个革命机构，而不是一支古典军队。
en: The second, or military, response to escalating catastrophe came in the immediate wake of Brest-Litovsk. It consisted of replacing the people’s militia of Red Guards that had been formed in 1917 with a Red Army based on the conventional formula of conscription, discipline, and a top-down chain of command.

The key measure—conscription—was introduced on April 22, and Trotsky redeployed his talents from diplomacy to war as Commander in Chief of the new revolutionary institution. For the Red Army, despite the return to hierarchy and discipline, remained a revolutionary institution, not a classical army.

zh: 布列斯特之前与德国人打交道的经验，以及五月之后白卫运动的发展，都表明一支由选举产生军官的业余志愿部队根本无法保障生存。战争是一门技术职业，需要职业军官来从事。这样的军官只能迅速从旧帝国军队的行列中抽调，但这些先生们不可信任。于是托洛茨基放手征召他们，并在他们身边配备政治委员团，其职责是在所有命令上副署，说服红军士兵服从新军官，并向所有人灌输正确的阶级战争政治态度。于是，新生制度中另一个不可或缺的要素被创造出来：党监视员，使一切“资产阶级”技术专家服从社会主义革命的政治目的。
en: The experience with the Germans prior to Brest-Litovsk, and then the growth of the White movement after May, had demonstrated that an amateur, volunteer force with elected officers simply could not provide for survival. Warfare is a technical profession, and professional officers were necessary to wage it. Such officers could be drawn quickly only from the ranks of the old Imperial army, but these gentlemen could not be trusted. So Trotsky conscripted them freely and flanked them with a corps of political commissars whose role was to countersign all orders, to persuade the Red ranks to obey their new officers, and to indoctrinate everyone with a correct political attitude for class war. Thus was created another indispensable element of the nascent system: the Party monitor who would subordinate all “bourgeois” technical experts to the political purposes of socialist revolution.

zh: 尽管这种双重管理制度最初是为军队发展出来的，它却可以应用于社会中的任何职能，应用于一切经济和其他民用任务。最终，在成熟的苏维埃秩序中，党的代表或部门将监督工业经理、集体农庄主席、教育工作者、科学家、作家——实际上是一切人和一切事。这是因为党的使命是实现一种政治和意识形态愿景；它的职责不是在维持现代社会运转所必需的各项活动中发挥技术和专业专长。
en: Although this system of dual administration was first developed for the army, it could be applied to any function in society, to all economic and other civilian tasks. Eventually, in the mature Soviet order, Party representatives or departments would supervise industrial managers, collective farm chairmen, educators, scientists, writers—indeed, everybody and everything. This is because the mission of the Party was to realize a political and ideological vision; its vocation was not to exercise technical and professional competence in any of the activities necessary for the functioning of modern society.

zh: 党的目的与其所控制社会的功能需要之间的这种脱节，在苏维埃政权最初几年尤为尖锐；当时一个此前处于地下的密谋组织突然发现自己控制着一个不听话的国家组织。如果社会要运转，党就必须使用旧秩序中它在政治上无法信任的“资产阶级专家”。于是，1918年立即开始在所有领域、而不仅仅是军事领域征用这类专家。当然，随着时间推移，党会培养自己的“红色专家”，在他们身上技术能力与政治正确性将统一起来。但在一个漫长而不确定的时期，或者说直到社会主义到来之前，党的监视员、政委或政治军官是绝对必要的。
en: This discrepancy between Party purposes and the functional needs of the society it controlled was particularly acute during the first years of Soviet power, when a hitherto underground, conspiratorial organization suddenly found itself in control of a recalcitrant state organization. If society were to function at all, the Party would have to use “bourgeois specialists” from the old order whom it could not trust politically. And the impressment of such specialists in all fields, not just the military, began immediately in 1918. In time, of course, the Party would train its own “Red specialists,” in whom technical competence and political correctness would be united. But for a lengthy and indeterminate period, or until socialism had arrived, the Party monitor, commissar, or political officer was an absolute necessity.

zh: 这种意识形态控制的需要，是党机关掌握社会中任何重要岗位任命权的萌芽；这种任命权构成了后来所称干部职务名称表制度（
）的核心。这种双重管理因此意味着“市民社会”的终结——在政权最后岁月里，苏联异见者用这个术语来指称一切能够独立于国家进行自组织的团体。这种控制方式成为党国的运作本质，是职能性的、政府的或“苏维埃”官僚机构在幕后受到一个平行的、不受问责的、拥有真正决策权的党行政机关监视的手段。
en: This need for ideological control was the germ of the Party apparat’s right of appointment to any functional post of importance in society, a right that defined a system later known as the

. Such dual administration thus spelled the end of “civil society”—a term which in the twilight years of the regime Soviet dissidents used to designate all groups capable of self-organization independent of the state. This mode of control became the operational essence of the Party-state, the means whereby the functional, governmental, or “Soviet” bureaucracy was monitored from behind the scenes by a parallel and unaccountable Party administration that had the real power of decision.

zh: 这个新制度的第一个巨大成功，是建立了一支有效的红军——所谓有效，是与白卫军相比，而不是与第一次世界大战的正规军相比。总而言之，在内战过程中，约有六百万人被征入红军（其中农民显然远多于工人）。这些人中约有三百万开小差或消失，回到他们被强征入伍的村庄。根据托洛茨基自己的估计，总数中只有约五十万到六十万人可以当作有效战斗力量使用。其中，工人出身的士兵最守纪律，对革命最忠诚——当时被称为军队的“红血球”。在冲突过程中，从这个群体中选拔出来并训练为军官的学员，开始逐渐取代沙皇时期的留任者。红军就这样成为新政权招募新人的主要来源。与此同时，随着民用经济停摆、工厂减产或完全关闭，军队在很大程度上吸收了无产阶级。
en: The first great success of this new system was the creation of an effective Red Army—effective, that is, in comparison with the White forces, not with the regular armies of the First World War. All told, in the course of the Civil War some six million men were conscripted into the Red Army (obviously, rather more of them were peasants than workers). Of these, some three million deserted or disappeared back into the villages from whence they had been dragooned. According to Trotsky’s own estimate, only around five hundred thousand or six hundred thousand of the total could be used as an effective fighting force. Of these, soldiers of worker background were the most disciplined and the most committed to the Revolution—the “red corpuscles” of the army, as they were called at the time. In the course of the conflict, cadets taken from this group and trained as officers began to progressively replace the holdovers from the tsarist period. In this manner the Red Army became a major source of recruitment of new men for the new regime. At the same time, the army largely absorbed the proletariat as the civilian economy ground to a halt and factories slowed production or closed altogether.

zh: 这支匆忙拼凑、结构拙劣、社会成分流动的力量，很难是欧洲正规军的对手——比如说，如果德国人再次侵入这个国家，或者西方盟国真的派出一支像样的远征军。但它足以击退同样临时拼凑、意识形态动力更弱、流动性更强的白卫军。当然，这才是关键所在。
en: This hastily improvised, poorly structured, and socially fluid force would hardly have been a match for a regular European army—say, if the Germans had advanced once again into the country, or if the Western Allies had ever landed a serious expeditionary force. But it was enough to fend off the equally improvised, less ideologically motivated, and even more fluid White armies. And this, of course, was what counted.

zh: 不过，如果把布尔什维克关于内战是一场阶级斗争、红色无产阶级对抗资产阶级和封建白卫军的修辞太当真，那也是个错误。从制度上看，使内战得以发生的，是旧帝国军队军官团内部的分裂：一批军官为新苏维埃国家工作，而在他们许多人眼中，这仍然是一个俄国国家；另一批军官则为重建某种类似传统俄罗斯帝国的东西而战——那个帝国“统一而不可分割”。简言之，在内战战场上，我们面对的既有两个敌对的国家权力或初生国家权力，也有两个社会阶级；前者并不比后者次要。苏维埃党国尽管怀有意识形态统治的抱负，却是一个在战斗中孕育的国家权力，只不过是一种全新类型的国家权力。
en: Still, it would be a mistake to take too literally Bolshevik rhetoric about the Civil War being a class struggle, with the Red proletariat pitted against the bourgeois and feudal Whites. Institutionally, what made the Civil War possible was a split within the officer corps of the old Imperial army: One group of officers worked for the new Soviet state, which, in the eyes of many of them, was still a Russian state; another group fought to reestablish something resembling the traditional Russian Empire, “one and indivisible.” In short, on the battlefields of the Civil War we are dealing as much with two rival state powers, or incipient state powers, as with two social classes. The Soviet Party-state, for all its ideocratic aspirations, was a state power in militant gestation, albeit a state power of a radically new type.

zh: 这两个俄国帝国初生继承国之间的激烈较量持续了十八个月，从1918年中期到1919年底。
在此期间，苏维埃政权三次处于致命危险之中。第一次，如前所见，是1918年夏天，德国人占领了西部和南部，白卫军从东部推进。第二次是1919年春天，高尔察克海军上将率军从西伯利亚向新首都莫斯科推进。第三次是当年秋天，邓尼金将军从乌克兰推进到距首都两百公里以内，尤登尼奇将军则从爱沙尼亚向彼得格勒进军。
en: The acute period of the contest between these two incipient successor states to the Russian Empire lasted eighteen months, from mid-1918 to the end of 1919.

During this time the Soviet regime was in mortal danger on three occasions. The first, as we have seen, was the summer of 1918, when the Germans occupied the west and the south, and the Whites advanced from the east. The second was the spring of 1919, when Admiral Kolchak advanced out of Siberia towards the new capital, Moscow. And the third occasion was the fall of that year, when General Denikin advanced from Ukraine to within two hundred kilometers of the capital, and General Yudenich moved on Petrograd from Estonia.

zh: 这里不是详述武装斗争曲折经过的地方；我们关心的是战争对苏维埃党国发展的影响。只需说，布尔什维克的胜利绝非命中注定。在刚才提到的三个致命危险时刻，如果偶然事件转向另一方向——比如说，如果1919年高尔察克和邓尼金同时而不是相隔五个月向莫斯科推进——那么布尔什维克的军事失败、因而政治崩溃，就会像1918年捷克事件期间一样完全可以想象。偶然性显然是这件事没有发生的一个原因。
en: This is not the place to enter into the vicissitudes of the armed struggle; our concern here is with the impact of the war on the development of the Soviet Party-state. Suffice it to say that Bolshevik success was by no means foreordained. At each of the three moments of mortal danger just mentioned, if contingent events had taken a different turn—if, say, Kolchak and Denikin in 1919 had advanced on Moscow simultaneously rather than five months apart—Bolshevik military defeat, and hence political collapse, would have been as wholly conceivable as during the Czech episode of 1918. Chance, obviously, was one reason this did not occur.

zh: 另一个偶然因素，是德国人在西线输掉了战争。因为如果他们在1918年春天突破到海峡港口和巴黎——他们几乎成功了——他们就可以自由地恢复被布列斯特和约中断的东进胜利进军，而杂牌红军几乎无法阻挡他们。在所有可能让俄国避免布尔什维主义的假设情景中，这也许是最“现实”的一个。然而，由于显而易见的原因，西方民主国家的历史学家从不倾向于考虑它，尽管它还会顺带让希特勒变得多余。
en: And another element of contingency was that the Germans lost the war in the West. For if they had broken through to the Channel ports and Paris in the spring of 1918—as they almost succeeded in doing—they then would have been free to resume their victorious eastward advance interrupted by the peace of Brest-Litovsk, and the ragtag Red Army could hardly have stopped them. Of all the hypothetical scenarios that might have permitted Russia to avoid Bolshevism, this is perhaps the most “realistic.” Yet, for obvious reasons, historians in the Western democracies have never been prone to contemplate it, even though it would have made Hitler superfluous into the bargain.

zh: 但布尔什维克得以幸存也有结构性原因。第一，他们拥有以莫斯科为中心向外辐射的内线交通优势，而白卫军在外围作战。第二，国际主义的红军说起来很奇怪，却可以显得是俄国爱国者，因为他们不受外国干涉大国支配。第三，尽管农民（现在常被称为“绿军”）因红军征粮而开始憎恨他们，却更害怕白卫军，因为后者的回归往往伴随着地主权力的恢复。结果，当敌对的红军和白军相继经过他们的田地时，农民对红军有微弱的偏好，因此在白军后方发动反抗。
正是这一因素尤其使邓尼金在1919年失败，让布尔什维克得以最终接管乌克兰，从而总体上完成胜利。
en: But there were structural reasons for the Bolsheviks’ survival as well. First, they had the advantage of interior lines of communication radiating out from Moscow, whereas the Whites were operating on the periphery. Second, the internationalist Reds oddly enough could appear to be Russian patriots because they were not beholden to foreign interventionist powers. Third, although the peasants (now often called the “greens”) had come to detest the Reds because of their requisitions of grain, they feared the Whites even more because the latter’s return often brought with it the restoration of the landowners’ power. As a consequence, as competing Red and White armies passed successively over their fields, the peasants had a marginal preference for the Reds and therefore revolted behind White lines.
It was this factor, in particular, that undid Denikin in 1919, allowing the Bolsheviks to definitively take over Ukraine and thus wrap up their victory overall.

zh: 但比这些具体因素更重要的是布尔什维克更强的组织能力——建立契卡，围绕政治委员构建红军，把苏维埃国家变成党的单纯机关。这种组织能力源自他们为社会主义这一超越性事业而追求权力垄断的意识形态动力。因此，临时政府无法治理的地方，布尔什维克掌权仅八个月就已迅速走向全面统治。面对同样曾摧毁临时政府的苏维埃离心倾向、工人无纪律和农民无政府状态，布尔什维克竭尽专政机构的全部力量予以反击，力图控制住他们前一年的鼓动所帮助释放的离心力量。
en: But even more important than these specific factors was the Bolsheviks’ superior capacity for organization—in building the Cheka, in structuring the Red Army around the political commissar, and in turning the Soviet state into a mere apparat of the Party. This capacity for organization derived from their ideological drive for a monopoly of power in the transcendent cause of socialism. Thus, where the Provisional Government had been unable to govern, the Bolsheviks after only eight months in power were well on their way to becoming a total government. Against the same forces of soviet fractiousness, worker indiscipline, and peasant anarchy that had destroyed the Provisional Government, the Bolsheviks fought back with every nerve of their dictatorship to bring under control the centrifugal forces their agitation of the previous year had helped unleash.

zh: 共产主义政策——不仅1917—1919年的俄国，而且此后全世界——的巨大悖论在于：它在野时是无政府主义的，在掌权时是极权主义的，而且它看不出两者之间有任何矛盾。事实上，在布尔什维克的逻辑中并无矛盾：他们做无政府主义者，是为了粉碎旧的资本主义世界；他们做独裁者，是为了建设新的社会主义世界。在这两个阶段，他们都有权——事实上是有义务——在政策上采取总体主义，因为在这两个阶段他们都是历史逻辑的载体和普遍阶级的先锋。简言之，解释布尔什维克既善于瓦解又善于重组的那种无情能力的，是他们的意识形态狂热。在这一点上，白卫军永远无法竞争。
en: The great paradox of Communist policy, not just in Russia during 1917-1919 but throughout the world thereafter, was that it was anarchist in opposition and totalitarian in power, and it saw no contradiction between the two. Indeed, in the Bolsheviks’ logic there was no contradiction: they were anarchist in order to pulverize the old, capitalist world, and dictatorial in order to build a new, socialist world. In both phases they had the right, in fact the obligation, to be totalistic in their policy because in both they were the vehicle of the logic of history and the vanguard of the universal class. In short, what explains the Bolsheviks’ ruthless capacity for both disorganization and reorganization is their ideological fanaticism. And in this the Whites could never compete.

zh: 共产主义者由意识形态驱动的组织和国家建设能力，在内战期间最说明问题的表现是在经济战线，以及那些后来被命名为战时共产主义的政策中。正是在这个领域，党国、它的政治警察和它的新式军队最终得以发挥作用；因为重塑经济将是建设社会主义的主要手段，从而实现这个制度的最终目的。而关于这个时期经济纲领的史学争论也最为激烈。
en: Where the Communist capacity for ideologically driven organization and state-building came through most tellingly during the Civil War was on the economic front and in those policies later baptized War Communism. It is in this area that the Party-state, its political police, and its new model army found their ultimate application; for remolding the economy would be the chief means for building socialism, and thus accomplishing the final purpose of the system. And it is on the economic programs of this period that the historiographical debate is most intense.

zh: 争论的焦点如下。尽管社会主义革命尚未扩展到欧洲其余地区，在战时共产主义的三年里，苏维埃政权（至少在意图上和纸面上）一路走到国家对经济的全面控制，并建设其领导人当时径称为共产主义——不带任何限定词——的东西。这一切完全违背了正当的、“正统的”马克思主义，也违背了布尔什维克自己最初宣布的意图。然后，在1921年，他们突然放弃这条路线，承认它过早且错误。布尔什维克把错误归咎于内战紧急状态，开始把最近的过去称为“战时”共产主义；与此同时，他们启动了一项基于半市场经济的“新经济政策”，即 NEP。
en: What is at issue is this. Even though the socialist revolution had not yet spread to the rest of Europe, in the three years of War Communism the Soviet regime went all the way (at least in intention and on paper) to full state control of the economy and the building of what its leaders then simply called Communism—without any qualifying adjective. All of this was quite contrary to proper, “orthodox” Marxism as well as to the Bolsheviks’ own originally proclaimed intentions. Then, in 1921, they brusquely abandoned this course, which they now admitted had been premature and mistaken. Attributing the error to the Civil War emergency, the Bolsheviks took to calling the recent past “War” Communism; at the same time, they launched a New Economic Policy, or the NEP, based on a semimarket economy.

zh: 那么，大问题就是：这两条路线中，哪一条才是布尔什维克通向社会主义的真正政策？一个推论问题是：战时共产主义究竟是由环境压力造成的偏离，还是表达布尔什维克基本愿望的意识形态事业？抑或它是环境与意识形态的共同产物？大多数历史评论在后者那种难有定论的中间道路与主张环境优先之间摇摆。但总体而言，西方史学尽可能快地处理这个痛苦时期，以便聚焦于据称更有希望的新经济政策年代。
en: The great question, then, is which of these two courses was the Bolsheviks’ true policy for reaching socialism. A corollary question is whether War Communism was an aberration caused by the pressure of circumstances or an ideologically driven enterprise that expressed the Bolsheviks’ basic aspirations. Or was War Communism the product of both circumstance and ideology? Most historical commentary has wavered between the latter, inconclusive middle way and the assertion of the primacy of circumstances. But by and large Western historiography deals with this painful period as quickly as possible in order to focus on the allegedly more promising years of the NEP.

zh: 然而，这件事对理解整个苏联历史关系重大。如果战时共产主义的残暴实践是布尔什维克的真正政策，那么合乎逻辑的结论就是：这个政权的整个未来确实如其实际结果那样黯淡；尤其是，斯大林于是显得是列宁的合法继承人。但如果战时共产主义是由战争偶然性造成的对列宁主义的偏离，那么就有可能把此后苏联历史的大部分视为“偏离”；斯大林被逐出真正的正典，而苏联事业被推定具有最终具有人道面孔的潜力。的确，戈尔巴乔夫的
本应正是这样的顶点。
en: Yet the stakes in this matter are very high for understanding the whole of Soviet history. If the brutal practices of War Communism were the true Bolshevik policy, then it is only logical that the whole future of the regime was as bleak as it in fact turned out to be; in particular, Stalin then appears as the legitimate heir of Lenin. But if War Communism was an aberration from Leninism caused by the contingency of war, then it is possible to view most of subsequent Soviet history as an “aberration”; Stalin is expunged from the true canon, and the Soviet enterprise is presumed to have had a potential for ending up with a human face. Indeed, Gorbachev’s
was supposed to have been just such a culmination.

zh: 如前所述，在掌权的最初八个月里，布尔什维克有时把他们的经济政策称为国家资本主义。新政府相信，在欧洲革命之前试图在俄国建设完整社会主义为时过早，但也不能允许俄国的资本主义保持原封不动。国家资本主义是迫使资产阶级为工人国家服务的工具。
en: As noted earlier, during their first eight months in power, the Bolsheviks at times referred to their economic policy as state capitalism. Believing that it would be premature to attempt building full socialism in Russia before the European revolution, the new government nonetheless could not permit capitalism in Russia to remain unadulterated. State capitalism was the vehicle whereby the bourgeoisie was supposed to be made to serve the workers’ state.

zh: 事实上，这一进程是通过一种辩证法展开的：事件促使采取激烈行动，然后意识形态又把这些行动进一步激进化。于是，当国家银行的职员拒绝向新政府提供资金时，武装支队于1917年11月7日占领银行并将其国有化。接着意识形态接管了，五天后所有私人银行被国有化，所有外债被废除。然而这些行动只是为政权招来新的国内外敌人，从而使经济问题更加严重——于是又促使采取进一步激烈行动。
en: In fact, this process developed through a dialectic where events prompted drastic action and then ideology radicalized these actions still further. Thus, when the employees of the State Bank refused to provide the new government with funds, armed detachments occupied the Bank on November 7, 1917, and nationalized it. Then ideology took over and five days later all private banks were nationalized and all foreign debts repudiated. Yet these actions only earned the regime new enemies, both foreign and domestic, thereby making its economic problems still worse—and so prompting further drastic action.

zh: 国家资本主义的这一初始阶段，在12月2日创建最高国民经济委员会时得到了最充分的表现，其俄文缩写为 Vesenkha（最高国民经济委员会）。这个机构负责组织、协调和规范“贸易与工业、粮食供应、农业、财政和工会”等人民委员部的活动——简言之，一切与经济有关的事务。
很快，最高国民经济委员会设立了称为
（总局）的部门，处理从纺织到冶金的各个工业分支；到春天，一个庞大的官僚机构已经出现，发布越来越详细的法令，规范它名义上控制的活动。因此，早在布列斯特和约和重大危机开始之前，对信贷的国家控制和官僚式协调——如果还算不上计划——已经在原则上建立起来。这首先是人们可以期望一个社会主义政府为保护劳动者利益、对抗已被击败的剥削者而采取的最低限度行动；这也是应对日益混乱局面的实际必要。
en: This initial phase of state capitalism received its fullest expression on December 2 with the creation of a Supreme Council of the National Economy, known by its Russian abbreviation as Vesenkha. This body was charged with organizing, coordinating, and regulating the activities of the commissariats dealing with “trade and industry, food supplies, agriculture, finance, and trade unions”—in short, everything connected with the economy.
Very soon Vesenkha created departments, called

, to deal with the various branches of industry, from textiles to metallurgy; and by the spring a sizeable bureaucracy had emerged to issue ever more detailed decrees regulating the activities over which it had nominal control. Thus, well before Brest-Litovsk and the onset of major crisis, state control of credit and bureaucratie coordination, if not as yet planning, had been established in principle. This was, first of all, the minimum that a socialist government could be expected to do to defend the interests of the toilers against their now defeated exploiters; it was also a practical necessity to cope with an increasingly chaotic situation.

zh: 国家干预的势头从1918年春天的危机中获得了强大推动。一个异常严酷的冬天加速了1917年已经开始的经济崩溃，而布列斯特和约造成的乌克兰粮食、铁和煤的丧失，又使这一进程恶化。到四五月间，城市的粮食状况已变得绝望：农民现在没有积极性为市场生产，因为他们换来的只是越来越不值钱的卢布，而且还没有消费品可买。
因此列宁颁布了“面包十字军”和“粮食专政”，这项政策由供应人民委员部在契卡协助下实施，针对“囤积者”和“富农”。到六月，如前所述，这个纲领已变成由“贫农委员会”（Kombedy）进行的“乡村阶级斗争”。
en: The momentum of state intervention received a mighty impetus from the crises of the spring of 1918. An exceptionally severe winter had accelerated the economic collapse that was already under way in 1917, but the process was now aggravated by the loss of Ukrainian grain, iron, and coal as a result of Brest-Litovsk. By April-May the food situation in the cities had become desperate: The peasants now had no incentive to produce for the market, where they received only increasingly worthless rubles with which, moreover, there were no consumer goods to buy.

Lenin therefore decreed a “crusade for bread” and a “food dictatorship,” a policy to be implemented by the Supply Commissariat with the aid of the Cheka and directed against “hoarders” and “kulaks.” By June, as already noted, this program had become “class warfare in the villages” waged by the “Committees of the Village Poor,” or Kombedy.

zh: 随着这项新政策和这些新标签，列宁1917年10月的土地法令暴露了它一直以来的真相：一种为党掌权铺路的权宜之计；同样，布尔什维克对农民的真正态度终于开始显现。当然，官方上政权仍将是“工人和农民的革命联盟”——列宁称之为
（结合）——以无处不在的锤子和镰刀为象征。但即便在十月，农民至多也只是革命扩大了的普遍阶级中一个非常初级的成员。在布尔什维克看来，他们只有作为一种被剥削、因而具有破坏性的力量，才有资格与工人“结盟”。除此之外，布尔什维克把他们视为一个落后的阶级，不可能有建设性的社会主义愿望。只有无产阶级，作为现代和技术阶级，才能成为进步的承担者。
en: With this new policy, and these new labels, Lenin’s Decree on Land of October 1917 was revealed for what it had always been: an expedient to ease the Party’s way to power; by the same token, the Bolsheviks’ real attitude toward the peasantry at last began to emerge. Officially, of course, the regime would remain a “revolutionary alliance of workers and peasants”—what Lenin called the

—symbolized by the omnipresent hammer and sickle. But even in October, the peasants had been at most a very junior member of the Revolution’s extended universal class. In the Bolshevik view, they were eligible for “alliance” with the workers only as an exploited, and therefore a disruptive, force. Otherwise, the Bolsheviks regarded them as a retrograde class incapable of constructive, socialist aspirations. The proletariat, as the modern and technological class, alone could be the bearer of progress.

zh: 因此，在革命后的局势中，
两个伙伴的道路只能分道扬镳。这首先在实践中成真；农民一旦得到土地，就对列宁的革命失去兴趣。正如他们在1918年春天、当党改名共产党并开始征粮时常说的：“我们拥护布尔什维克，但反对共产党人。”在布尔什维克对其“盟友”的政策中也是如此；党现在开始区分农民的各个亚阶层，只有其中最受压迫者才留在联盟之内。
en: Thus in the post-revolutionary situation, the course of the two partners in the

could only diverge. This was true first in practice; once the peasants had the land, they lost interest in Lenin’s revolution. As they often put it in the spring of 1918, when the Party changed its name to Communist and started requisitioning grain: “we are for the Bolsheviks, but against the Communists.” This was true also in the Bolsheviks’ policy toward their “allies”; the Party now began to distinguish among subclasses of the peasantry, only the most oppressed of which remained within the alliance.

zh: 这种新做法也许是布尔什维克制造出来的意识形态对现实生活的最大胜利。在马克思主义历史理论中，农民没有有意义的位置；他们是一个无可救药的“尴尬”阶级，如果历史要到达现代性，他们只适合被消灭。俄国马克思主义者通过一种取自城市世界社会学的阶级斗争范畴网格，抹平这个尴尬阶级的特殊性，从而解决了这个问题。这一过程始于1890年代，当时马克思主义者反驳民粹派，论证资本主义已经来到俄国；其主要后果之一，是农民内部阶级分化的发展使村社遭到破坏。列宁1899年的《俄国资本主义的发展》是这场争论中的关键著作。
en: This new approach represents perhaps the greatest triumph of ideology over real life produced by the Bolsheviks. In the Marxist theory of history there is no meaningful place for peasants; they are an irredeemably “awkward” class, fit only for elimination if history is to reach modernity. Russian Marxists solved the problem of this awkward class by obliterating its particularities under a grid of class-struggle categories taken from their sociology of the urban world. This process began in the 1890s when the Marxists argued against the Populists that capitalism had already arrived in Russia; among its chief consequences was the destruction of the village commune through the creation of class differentiation among the peasants. Lenin’s
in 1899 was a key item in this debate.

zh: 根据列宁的说法，资本主义发展的结果是村庄分裂为三个阶级。顶层是资产阶级的功能等价物：富农（kulak，源自“拳头”一词，是村中高利贷者的传统称呼）。中间是小资产阶级的替身，即
，中农。底层是无产阶级的替身，即
，贫农，他们作为雇工受富农剥削。因此，富农成为俄国乡村“资本主义”的先锋。
en: The result of the development of capitalism, according to Lenin, was a division of the village into three classes. At the top, there was a functional equivalent of the bourgeoisie: the kulaks (from the word for “fist,” the traditional term for village usurer). In the middle there was a surrogate petty bourgeoisie, the
, or middle peasants. And at the bottom, there was a stand-in for the proletariat, the
, or poor peasants, who were exploited as laborers by the kulaks. The latter, therefore, became the cutting edge of “capitalism” in rural Russia.

zh: 尽管农民不同于马克思主义理论家，很少写关于乡村社会学的书，但我们确实知道，上述一切与村庄中真实而微小的社会分化，或与农民对自己处境的看法，几乎没有关系。1917年后，所谓富农不过是一个有一匹马和三头牛、一年中雇几个较穷农民帮忙的庄稼汉（muzhik）。而且，农民认为这种相互依赖关系很正常；较有进取心的农民实际上是中农群众的榜样，而不是阶级敌人。对各个阶层的农民来说，真正的敌人是村庄之外的世界：国家、城市，以及1917年之后的党。
en: Although peasants, unlike Marxist theorists, rarely write books about rural sociology, we do know that all of the foregoing bears little relationship to the real though minimal social differentiations within the village, or to the peasants own view of their situation. After 1917, a kulak was no more than a muzhik with one horse and three cows who would hire a couple of poorer peasants for part of the year. The peasants, moreover, found such relationships of interdependence normal; the more enterprising peasant was in fact a model for the middle peasant mass, not a class enemy. For peasants of all levels, the real enemy was the world outside the village: the state, the city, and, after 1917, the Party.

zh: 然而，尽管列宁的乡村社会学本身荒谬，它对于建设党所谓的社会主义却有一项重大功能；它提供了不可或缺的政治手段，使党得以利用并最终征服村庄。这个目标——而不仅仅是收粮——才是乡村阶级斗争的真正含义，一场由农村无产阶级
及其城市大哥即党组成的新“联盟”进行的战争。只有凭借这种意识形态幻觉，党才能转而对付其
中较大的乡村一翼，同时仍然问心无愧地相信，它代表着农民的“真正”利益。
en: Yet, absurd though Lenin’s rural sociology is in itself, it had a major function for building what the Party called socialism; it furnished the indispensable political means that permitted the Party to exploit, and ultimately to subjugate, the village. This objective, not merely grain collection, was the real meaning of class warfare in the village, a war to be waged by the new “alliance” of the rural proletariat, the
, and its urban big brother, that is, the Party. Only with this ideological illusion could the Party turn on the larger, rural wing of its
and still believe, in all good conscience, that it represented the peasants’ “real” interests.

zh: 因此，到1918年夏天，意识形态、政治和警察机制已在俄国农业中取代了市场。直到1921年初，也就是内战结束后很久，粗糙的意识形态—政治乃至军事措施都以这种或那种形式代替市场。这一模式中的唯一变化出于权宜之计。于是，“村中穷人”以乡村阶级斗争为名掠夺“富农余粮”的做法，被证明对生产极具破坏性，并在政治上使农民疏远，以至于1919年初政权不得不放弃它。但它被同样原始的东西取代：由无产阶级支队或契卡进行国家征粮，这一制度称为
（余粮征集制）。有时征粮以消费品作为交换，有时则干脆在枪口下没收；但两种情况下都是强制性的。
en: Thus, by the summer of 1918, ideological, political, and police mechanisms had replaced the market in Russian agriculture. In one guise or another, crude ideo-political and, indeed, military measures would substitute for the market up to the beginning of 1921, that is, until well after the end of the Civil War. The only variations within this pattern were due to expediency. Thus, the plunder of “kulak surpluses” by the “village poor” under the guise of class warfare in the countryside proved so disruptive of production, and so alienated the peasantry politically, that early in 1919 the regime had to abandon it. But it was replaced by something just as primitive: the state requisition of grain by proletarian detachments or the Cheka, a system known as
. At times the requisition was in exchange for consumer goods, and at other times it was simply confiscated at gunpoint; but in both cases it was forced.

zh: 然而这并不是布尔什维克农业政策的全部。他们的最终目标是通过向村庄引入“合理的”大规模机械化生产，消灭“城乡矛盾”。作为这一农业未来的第一幅粗略草图，一些前贵族庄园被改造成国营农场，即sovkhozy（国营农场），农民在那里作为领薪工人劳动。这个实验当时完全失败，但它仍然显示了，如果布尔什维克一旦有手段实施其合理农业组织的理想，他们真正想对不听话的农民群众做什么。然而与此同时，他们依靠
生存。但这项政策除了满足党生存的最低需要之外，也谈不上成功，因为那一点点余粮越来越多地流向黑市。更糟的是，
对生产的破坏如此之大，以至于它与干旱一起成为1921—1922年灾难性饥荒的主要原因。
en: Yet this was not the whole of the Bolsheviks’ agrarian policy. Their ultimate aim was the abolition of the “contradiction between town and country” by the introduction of “rational,” large-scale mechanized production into the villages. As a first rough sketch of this agrarian future, a number of former gentry estates were transformed into state farms, or sovkhozy, where the peasants labored as salaried workers. This experiment was a complete failure at the time, but it nonetheless showed what the Bolsheviks really wanted to do with the recalcitrant peasant mass if ever they had the means to implement their ideal of rational agrarian organization. In the meantime, however, they relied on

to survive. But this policy, too, was not really a success beyond meeting the minimal needs of Party survival, for what little surplus grain there was went increasingly to the black market. Worse still,
was so disruptive of production that it was a major cause, together with drought, of the disastrous famine of 1921-1922.

zh: 当时俄国的任何政府都会被迫采取某种强制政治行动，以代替一个无法避免崩溃的市场；事实上，白卫军在其控制区也实行过类似但没那么激烈的做法。然而布尔什维克行动值得注意的是它的意识形态性质，这一特征使它系统化、无所不包，并与政权的最终目的——社会主义——逻辑相连。布尔什维克不仅仅是在极度贫困时期养活其支持者；他们粗俗而常常暴力的活动——事实上与偷窃相差无几——被提升为通向新世界不可或缺的一步。乡村阶级斗争这种愚蠢做法只会使供应状况更糟，但这无关紧要：它助长了信念，帮助红色运动继续下去。因此，尽管战时共产主义是在乡村为回应农民退出市场而启动的，但通过以政治占有资源取代市场，布尔什维克正在完成社会主义本应完成的事情。
en: Any government in Russia at the time would have been driven to some measure of coercive political action as a substitute for a market whose collapse could not be avoided; indeed, the Whites engaged in similar, though less drastic, practices in the areas they controlled. What is noteworthy about the Bolshevik action, however, is its ideological nature, a characteristic that made it systematic, all-embracing, and logically linked to the ultimate purpose of the regime—socialism. The Bolsheviks were not simply feeding their constituents at a time of desperate penury; their vulgar and often violent activity—in fact, it was not very different from theft—was raised to the level of an indispensable step towards a New World. Small matter that the inane practice of class warfare in the villages only made the supply situation worse: It fueled conviction and helped to keep the Red movement going. Thus, although War Communism was launched in the countryside in response to the peasants’ withdrawal from the market, by replacing that market with the political appropriation of resources, the Bolsheviks were accomplishing what socialism was supposed to do anyway.

zh: 工业中的战时共产主义，同样始于对工人“自发性”破坏力量的回应。1918年春天，面对粮食危机，工人开始把生产转向任何可以换取食物的商品。于是“工人控制工业”常常从监督管理层演变为直接接管工厂，再演变为地方“国有化”。由于其中一些工厂属于德国人，这种情况可能给德军提供进一步干预的借口。同样具有威胁性的是，这种基层国有化否定了布尔什维克的权力。
en: War Communism in industry began as a similar response to the disruptive force of worker “spontaneity.” In the course of the spring of 1918, faced with the grain crisis, workers began to divert production to whatever goods could be bartered for food. Thus “workers’ control of industry” often evolved from supervision of management to outright takeover of the plant, and then to local “nationalization.” Since some of these plants were owned by Germans, the situation could offer the German army a pretext for further intervention. Just as threatening, this grass-roots nationalization negated Bolshevik power.

zh: 6月12日，政府颁布法令，将所有重工业普遍国有化。在接下来的六个月里，政府接连发布一系列法令，将轻工业、批发贸易、零售贸易、合作社，最终将国内每一个手工业或商业企业，直到只有五名雇员的企业，全部国有化。于是，再一次，一个始于回应事件挑战的进程获得了总体化的意识形态势头，至少在原则上把这个国家变成了一家单一的国家企业。
en: On June 12 the government decreed general nationalization by the state of all heavy industry. In the course of the next .six months, the government went on to issue a flurry of decrees nationalizing light industry, wholesale trade, retail trade, the cooperatives, and ultimately every last artisan or commercial enterprise in the country, down to those that had only five employees. Thus, once again, a process that began as a response to the challenge of events acquired a totalizing ideological momentum that left the country, in principle at least, as a single state enterprise.

zh: 可以想见，这种国家干预过度产生了非常混杂的结果。红军得到了装备和食物，但城市不断减少的人口连最起码的必需品都得不到。与此同时，制度的高度集中化，加上各
之间的内斗，实际上加剧了工业的紊乱。此外，国家对分配的控制完全无效：市场没有被压制，而是被赶入地下，变成非法。
en: As might be expected, this statist overkill produced very mixed results. Although the Red Army was equipped and fed, the dwindling population of the cities was not even minimally supplied with the bare necessities. At the same time, the hypercentralization of the system, in conjunction with internecine conflict among the
, actually contributed to industrial disorganization. In addition, state control of distribution was totally ineffective: the market was not suppressed but driven underground and into illegality.

zh: 然而，再一次，这些副作用无关紧要，因为某种重要得多的东西已经实现：工业和商业中的私有财产被根除，利润被废除；通过这些手段，“人剥削人”的基础被克服。同样重要的是，市场在最高国民经济委员会的政治指挥结构中得到了一个社会主义继承者。到1921年初，这个机构已经创建了一个负责长期经济协调的特别单位——Gosplan，即国家计划委员会；它当时几乎没有实际工作可做，却注定要在制度中扮演核心角色。因为按照“真实需要”而非利润和对“市场无政府状态”的依赖来“合理”安排经济活动，正是社会主义在长远上本应实现的目标，即便没有内战要打也是如此。
en: Yet, once again, small matter these side effects, for something much more important had been achieved: private property in industry and commerce had been eradicated and profit had been abolished; by these means, the bases for the “exploitation of man by man” had been overcome. Just as important, the market had received a socialist successor in the political command structure of Vesenkha. And by-early 1921 this agency had created a special unit for long-term economic coordination, Gosplan, or the State Planning Commission, which for the moment had little to do but was destined to play a central role in the system. For the “rational” ordering of economic activity in terms of “real needs”—not in terms of profit and reliance on the “anarchy of the market”—was what socialism was supposed to achieve in the long run, even if there had been no civil war to fight.

zh: 但如果私有财产、利润和市场都被压制了，那么就不需要货币了。恰巧，事件的势头以欧洲此前所见最极端的通货膨胀形式，无论如何正在消灭货币。这被视为历史进程已把俄国完全推出资本主义、送入社会主义的迹象，于是到1920年底，布尔什维克准备正式废除货币。
en: But if private property, profit, and the market had been suppressed, then there was no need for money. As it happened, the momentum of events, in the form of the most extreme inflation Europe had yet seen, was doing away with money anyway. This was taken as a sign that the course of history had propelled Russia fully out of capitalism and into socialism, and so by the end of 1920 the Bolsheviks were preparing to formally abolish money.

zh: 事实上，内战期间发生的是俄国生活的一场非凡原始化：工业生产近乎崩溃，前所未有地倒退到自然经济或物物交换经济，只是被最高国民经济委员会及其

的纸面法令勉强遮盖。这种原始化最极端的迹象，也许出现在战争获胜、党转向重建经济之后。托洛茨基当时主张，重建只要把在内战中带来胜利的方法搬到工业企业的运营中即可。这种“劳动军事化”（布哈林也为之辩护的纲领）字面意义上意味着像红军一样管理工业；事实上，有一段时间，军事单位被用来重新开放矿井和工厂，让铁路重新运转。的确，战争结束后数月，列宁和党内多数领导人都相信，战时共产主义的一般方法就是通向社会主义的正确方法，应当无限期继续下去。于是，在一场名副其实的意识形态谵妄中，本世纪最巨大的经济崩溃被变形为现实存在的共产主义，变身为光辉的未来——
（此时此地），这一愿景投射在布哈林和普列奥布拉任斯基一度著名的《共产主义ABC》中。
en: In fact, what had occurred during the Civil War was an extraordinary primitivization of Russian life: a near collapse of industrial production and an unprecedented reversion to a natural or barter economy barely plastered over with the paper decrees of Vesenkha and its

. Perhaps the most extreme indication of this primitivization came once the war was won and the Party turned to rebuilding the economy. Trotsky then advocated that reconstruction be carried out simply by transferring to the operation of the industrial plant the methods that had brought victory in the Civil War. This “militarization of labor” (a program also defended by Bukharin) meant literally running industry like the Red Army; in fact, for a time, military units were used to reopen mines and factories and to get the railroads running again. Indeed, Lenin and most of the Party leadership for months after the end of the war believed that the methods of War Communism in general were the right ones for arriving at socialism and should be continued indefinitely. Thus, in a veritable ideological delirium, the most colossal economic collapse of the century was transmogrified into really-existing Communism, the radiant future
, a vision projected in Bukharin’s and Preobrazhenskii’s once famous

zh: 第一季度报告
en: A FIRST-QUARTER REPORT

zh: 那么，关于环境与意识形态在产生这一离奇结果中的相对分量，我们应当得出什么结论？

首先，应当注意，战时共产主义的做法既早于冲突，也在冲突结束后继续存在。信贷国有化和国家控制基本框架最高国民经济委员会的建立，都早于布列斯特和约；而且，粮食专政这类经济阶级斗争措施，也在任何真正的战斗开始之前就已出现。甚至战时共产主义最激烈的措施——工业全面国有化、乡村阶级斗争和贫农委员会——也是在1918年晚春出现的，那无疑是一个大危机时刻，但尚未与白卫军发生真正冲突。持续的军事紧急状态出现在1919年，即高尔察克、邓尼金和尤登尼奇之年，而那当然也是
和整个城市经济国有化的时期。因此总体而言，军事紧急状态只能解释战时共产主义较小的一部分，解释它的加剧而非起源。所以至少我们必须选择那个难有定论的解决方案：环境与意识形态都在起作用——换句话说，安全的中间道路。
en: So what should we conclude with regard to the relative weight of circumstance and ideology in producing this bizarre result?

First, it should be noted that the practices of War Communism both antedated the conflict and continued after its conclusion. The nationalization of credit and the creation of the basic framework for state control, Vesenkha, preceded Brest-Litovsk; moreover, such measures of economic class warfare as the food dictatorship came before any serious fighting began. Even the most drastic measures of War Communism—the full nationalization of industry, class warfare in the villages, and Committees of the Village Poor—came in the late spring of 1918, at a time of great crisis, to be sure, but not yet of serious conflict with the Whites. The sustained military emergency came in 1919, the year of Kolchak, Denikin, and Yudenich, and this of course was the time of

and the nationalization of the entire urban economy. Thus, overall, the military emergency can account for only the lesser part of War Communism, and its intensification rather than its origins. So at the very least we must opt for the inconclusive solution that both circumstance and ideology were operative—in other words, the safe middle way.

zh: 但这种历史因果关系的复式记账法根本不是解决方案，因为现实并不是以这种分隔的方式运作的。相反，战时共产主义应当根据马克思主义“理论与实践统一”的关键原则来理解：意识形态与行动，或者说实践，是同一进程的两个方面。没有指导性概念就不可能有实际行动，而意识形态始终与政治生活本身同体。正是从这个黑格尔—马克思主义视角——毕竟，相关行动者最认真地对待这一视角——才能最好地评价他们1918—1921年的政策。
en: But this double-entry bookkeeping approach to historical causation is really no solution at all, for reality does not work in such compartmentalized fashion. Rather, War Communism should be understood in the light of the key Marxist principle of the “unity of theory and practice”: Ideology and action, or praxis, are two facets of the same process. There can be no practical action without a guiding concept, and ideology is always consubstantial with political life itself. It is from this Hegelo-Marxist perspective—which, after all, the actors in question took most seriously—that their policies of 1918-1921 can best be evaluated.

zh: 因此，如果断言在战时共产主义期间马克思主义只是为回应军事紧急状态而采取的行动提供事后合理化，或者像 E. H. 卡尔那样论证布尔什维克只是为了保住权力而做不得不做的事，我们就大错特错了。他们确实痴迷于保住权力。但真正的问题是，他们为什么如此热烈地想要权力；毕竟，列宁的党并不是某种把权力本身当作目的的廉价独裁政权。布尔什维克需要权力，以实现他们光辉的社会主义目标，而他们为保住权力而斗争的方式，也不断被权力所要服务的目的所塑造。于是，乡村阶级斗争既是养活军队的方式，也是向社会主义目标前进的手段。就这样，从一项紧急措施到另一项紧急措施，布尔什维克使自己相信，在“阶级斗争的热潮”中，他们同时而且辩证地摧毁着资本主义，并“锻造着”未来社会主义秩序的“制度”。于是，在内战中，普遍崩溃在他们的逻辑中也可以显得是一次大跃进。
en: We are therefore profoundly mistaken to assert that during War Communism Marxism served simply as an ex post facto rationalization for actions undertaken in response to the military emergency, or to argue, as did E. H. Carr, that the Bolsheviks simply did what they had to do to stay in power. Quite true, they were obsessed with preserving power. But the real question is why they wanted it so passionately; after all, the Party of Lenin was not some tin-horn dictatorship to which power was an end in itself. The Bolsheviks required power in order to achieve their luminous goal of socialism, and the manner in which they fought to preserve that power was constantly molded by the end it was to serve. Thus, class warfare in the villages was simultaneously a way to feed the army and a means to advance toward the goal of socialism. And so, from one such emergency measure to another, the Bolsheviks convinced themselves that in the “heat of the class struggle” they were simultaneously, and dialectically, destroying capitalism and “forging the institutions” of the coming socialist order. Thus the universal collapse of the Civil War could appear, in their logic, as a great leap forward.

zh: 如果我们把马克思主义视为一个意识形态总体，而不是一份程序要点的经院清单，那么这一切都相当符合马克思主义。意识形态不是人们从书本中查阅然后应用的一套戒律。它是一种包罗万象的心态，渗透到那些在非意识形态观察者看来互不相干、临时拼凑的行动和决定之中。于是，常被用来把战时共产主义说成偏离的一个论据是：马克思并没有明确阐述这样的社会主义纲领，据称他只关心对资本主义的批判。诚然，马克思确实拒绝为未来秩序提供详细蓝图，而他那些被斥为“乌托邦”的社会主义者却轻率地这样做了。不过，从他的否定性资本主义批判中，其社会主义的基本轮廓仍然相当清楚。
en: And all of this is quite Marxist if we see Marxism as an ideological totality rather than as a scholastic list of programmatic points. Ideology is not a set of precepts that people look up in a book and then apply. It is an all-encompassing mind-set that pervades actions and decisions that to nonideological observers appear disparate and ad hoc. Thus, one of the arguments frequently used to write off War Communism as an aberration is that no such program for socialism is explicitly set forth in Marx, who was allegedly concerned only with producing a critique of capitalism. And, to be sure, Marx did refuse to give any detailed blueprint for the future order, as was so rashly done by those socialists he branded “utopian.” Nonetheless, the basic outlines of his socialism are quite clear from his negative critique of capitalism.

zh: 最重要的是，私有财产和市场必须消失；货币也必须消失，它“来到世上时，每一个毛孔都滴着血”。整整几类人口——从“封建”贵族到“小资产阶级”民主派，甚至包括走入歧途的社会主义者——都必须被排除在选举权之外，或以某种方式受到镇压，因为他们是试图阻挡历史逻辑的反动派。特别是，必须通过消灭“乡村生活的愚昧”——即农民，这个套在人类脖子上的巨大“土豆口袋”——来终结落后的“城乡分工”。具体而言，这意味着乡村必须城市化，把农民变成农业工厂即集体农庄中的劳动者。
en: Above all, private property and the market would have to go; so too would money, “which came into the world dripping with blood through every pore.” Whole categories of the population—from “feudal” aristocrats to “petty bourgeois” democrats, and even errant socialists—would have to be excluded from the suffrage or in some manner repressed because they were reactionaries trying to hold back the logic of history. In particular, the retrograde “division of labor between town and country” would have to be ended by eliminating the “idiocy of rural life,” that is, the peasantry, that great “sack of potatoes” around the neck of mankind. Concretely, this meant that the countryside would have to he urbanized by making the peasants into laborers in agricultural factories, or collective farms.
