〔译注〕《资本论》中“每个毛孔”滴血与污秽的表述，其直接指称对象是资本；马克思在同一处引述奥热关于货币生来脸颊带血的说法。

zh: 这一切在马克思和恩格斯那里都相当明确，而他们在第二国际中的许多德国和奥地利追随者，通过较为详细地谈论集体农庄和集中计划，把事情说得更清楚。
同样，马克思只寥寥数次使用“无产阶级专政”这个对列宁如此核心的概念，这只有次要意义。马克思对强制的积极态度，通过大量对“革命是历史的火车头”或“暴力是历史的助产士”的颂扬而表露无遗。因此，他未来纲领的主要线索几乎无可怀疑：这是一个无所不包的国有化、集体化和计划化工程，想必将由历史逻辑来实现——而革命强制同样是那一“逻辑”的组成部分。
en: All of this is quite explicit in Marx and Engels, and many of their German and Austrian followers in the Second International made matters clearer still by talking in some detail of collective farms and centralized planning.

Similarly, it is of only secondary importance that Marx used the phrase “dictatorship of the proletariat,” a concept so central for Lenin, a mere handful of times. Marx made clear his positive attitude toward coercion by copious encomia to “revolutions as the locomotive of history,” or “violence as the midwife of history.” Thus, the main lines of his program for the future are hardly in doubt: It was an all-embracing project of nationalization, collectivization, and planning, presumably to be realized by the logic of history—and revolutionary coercion was also integral to that “logic.”

zh: 布尔什维克在战时共产主义下试图实施的，正是这样一个总体性的共产主义化纲领。至于历史的形式逻辑，他们把对更刻板方面的依赖留给孟什维克和西方社会民主党人，转而强调阶级斗争的意志论和强制力量。于是，布尔什维克把内战紧急状态的军事共产主义升级为一种战斗性的、千禧年主义的共产主义，一种被设计成要持久存在的共产主义。尽管有卡尔·考茨基和尤利·马尔托夫的责难，这项事业仍然可以说符合马克思主义深层结构的模式。列宁及其同事当时这样想是完全正确的，而当他们被迫开始新经济政策后否认自己的所作所为时，则有些言不由衷。他们确实是
的，因为他们的乌托邦实践已造成一场全国性灾难，威胁要摧毁党的权力。因此，他们暂时抛弃最大化纲领以保住权力，好让党活下去，改日再战。
en: It is just such a total program of communization that the Bolsheviks attempted to implement under War Communism. As for the formal logic of history, they left reliance on its more lockstep aspects to the Mensheviks and the Western Social Democrats, and emphasized instead the voluntaristic and coercive power of the class struggle. Thus the Bolsheviks escalated the military communism of the Civil War emergency into a militant and millenarian communism, one that was designed to endure. And despite the strictures of Karl Kautsky and Iulii Martov, this enterprise was legitimately in the mode of Marxism’s deeper structure. Lenin and his colleagues were quite right in thinking so at the time, and somewhat disingenuous in disowning their handiwork once they were forced to embark on the NEP. And they were indeed

, for their utopia in action had produced such a national disaster that it threatened to destroy the Party’s power. They therefore temporarily jettisoned their maximalist program in order to preserve that power, so that the Party might live to fight again another day.

zh: 尽管战时共产主义源于意识形态，但就实际而言，这场向未来的非凡跳跃之所以可能，是因为内战年代同样非凡的社会革命。这场革命采取的形式，是旧社会结构几乎完全的分解。这一进程始于1917年，并在内战年代不断恶化，直到1920年秋敌对行动结束才触底。
en: Though it was derived from ideology, as a practical matter the extraordinary leap into the future that was War Communism was made possible by the equally extraordinary social revolution of the Civil War years. This revolution took the form of the nearly complete decomposition of the old social fabric. This process had begun in 1917 and steadily worsened during the Civil War years, only reaching bottom with the end of hostilities in the fall of 1920.

zh: 这一结果与先前欧洲革命的模式彻底不同。在较早的革命中，旧秩序被推翻、尘埃落定之后，结果是某些社会群体上升了，另一些下降了；然而最终几乎所有群体仍然存在，因此社会仍保持多样化和分层。例如，1789年之后的法国，贵族和教士下降了，中产阶级和农民上升了；尽管社会结构发生了巨大变化，每个群体的地位也大大改变，但没有一个群体被完全消灭。
en: This outcome represented a radical departure from the pattern of previous European revolutions. In earlier revolutions, once the old order had been overthrown and the dust had settled, it turned out that some social groups had moved up in the world while others had moved down; almost all, however, were still there in the end, and thus society had remained diversified and stratified. In France after 1789, for example, the nobility and the clergy had moved down while the middle classes and the peasantry had moved up; although the structure of society had changed mightily, and the status of each group had changed greatly, none of them had been totally eliminated.

zh: 然而在1917年之后的俄国，非同寻常的事实是，“普通人”或“劳动群众”以上的一切社会群体都作为有凝聚力的团体被消灭了。贵族、教士、自由职业者、中产阶级或“资产阶级”——全都作为有组织的实体不复存在。旧俄国社会唯一留存的阶级，是它的体力劳动者阶级，即工人和农民。被剥夺群体中的大多数个人当然仍然活着，但他们的群体或阶级凝聚力已被摧毁。此外，这些个人在新秩序下受到法律歧视：被剥夺选举权，口粮减少。简言之，“市民社会”消失了，俄国社会只剩下一个基本上未分化的“劳动者”大众。
en: In Russia after 1917, however, the extraordinary fact is that all social groups above the “simple people,” or the “toiling masses,” were eliminated as cohesive bodies. The gentry, the clergy, the liberal professionals, the middle classes, or the “bourgeoisie”—all ceased to exist as organized entities. The only classes of the old Russian society that remained were those of its manual laborers, the workers and peasants. Most of the individuals in the dispossessed groups remained of course, but their group or class cohesion was destroyed. Moreover, these individuals were legally discriminated against under the new order: They were deprived of the suffrage and received reduced food rations. In short, “civil society” disappeared, and all that was left of Russian society was a largely undifferentiated mass of “toilers.”

zh: 这种空前的社会扁平化之所以发生，是因为与此前欧洲革命不同，私有财产被废除了。这在一定程度上是因为1917年之前财产本来就不那么普遍，大多数农民并不拥有自己的土地。私有财产的废除也得益于乡村和城市社会革命的原始力量。但在更大程度上，财产是因布尔什维克的蓄意政策而消失的。
en: This unprecedented social levelling occurred because, unlike in earlier European revolutions, private property had been abolished. This came about in part because property had not been all that widespread before 1917, since most of the peasantry did not own their land. The abolition of private property was also facilitated by the elemental forces of social revolution in both the countryside and the cities. But, in even larger part, property disappeared as the result of deliberate Bolshevik policy.

zh: 这一切的后果是，群众同他们从前的主人一样，在面对国家时被剥夺了任何施加政治影响的筹码。诚然，工人仍有工会，但1918年夏之后，这些组织被置于党之下。内战后，当所谓的“工人反对派”试图恢复工会，使其成为重建经济的组织力量时，他们在1921年第十次代表大会上被决定性地击败；经济控制权仍归党，工会则被彻底变成党的代理人。农民仍有传统的村社——1917年的农业革命甚至加强了它——在那里他们实际上管理着自己的大部分事务。但在与苏维埃国家的关系中，农民唯一的杠杆，要么是心怀怨愤地拒绝交粮，要么是起义。名义上构成苏维埃国家的工农苏维埃，事实上很大程度上是党意志的传送带。
en: The consequence of all this was that the masses, no less than their former masters, were deprived of any political leverage vis-à-vis the state. To be sure, the workers still had their unions, but after the summer of 1918 these organizations were subordinated to the Party. When, at the end of the Civil War, the so-called Workers’ Opposition attempted to revive the unions as the organizing force in rebuilding the economy, they were decisively defeated at the Tenth Congress in 1921; control of the economy remained with the Party, and the unions were definitively transformed into its agents. The peasants still had their traditional rural commune—which was even strengthened by the agrarian revolution of 1917—where they in fact managed most of their own affairs. But in their relations with the Soviet state, the peasants’ only leverage was either sullen refusal to cooperate in grain deliveries or revolt. The workers’ and peasants’ soviets, which nominally constituted the Soviet state, were in fact largely transmission belts of the Party’s will.

zh: 欧洲历史上从未发生过如此彻底的社会扁平化；从未有一个社会相对国家被如此彻底地解除武装。布尔什维克之所以能实现这一非凡业绩，只是因为革命前俄国社会的不成熟和脆弱。与西欧和中欧大多数国家不同，旧俄国缺乏一个古老市民社会的稳固结构，缺乏多元的根深蒂固的利益集团，也缺乏大批失去的将远多于锁链的人。特别是，旧俄国有太多农民，而他们在制度中的利害关系太少。这是帝国政权为何如此轻易崩溃、临时政府为何始终只是一个幽灵的重要原因。这也是布尔什维克为何能如此轻易夺取政权、为何能如此迅速地把战时共产主义的超现实幻想强加于国家的原因。根本不存在能够有效反对他们——也就是说，进行一场真正阶级斗争——的结构。
en: Never before in European history had such a radical social levelling occurred; never before had a society been so thoroughly disarmed vis-à-vis the state. The Bolsheviks were able to achieve this extraordinary feat only because of the immaturity and fragility of prerevolutionary Russian society. Unlike most countries of Western and Central Europe, old Russia lacked the solid structures of a venerable civil society, one with a plurality of entrenched vested interests and large masses of people who had much more to lose than their chains. In particular, old Russia had too many peasants with too little stake in the system. This is a major reason why the Imperial regime had collapsed so easily, and why the Provisional Government had never been more than a phantom. This is also why the Bolsheviks could seize power so easily, and why they could impose the surreal fantasy of War Communism on the country so quickly. There were simply no structures capable of opposing them effectively—that is, of putting up a real class struggle.

zh: 正是俄国市民社会根深蒂固的弱点，为共产主义的混合物提供了独特的俄国成分。共产主义的极权主义性质，不能被解释为传统俄国专制主义或东方专制的延续；苏维埃社会的集体主义性质，也不能被理解为传统俄国村社和农奴制社会关系的继续。在布尔什维克1917年后实际推行的政策中，很难找到任何这种从旧俄国到新俄国的传递机制；相反，很容易在列宁主义政党的社会主义目的中找到这些政策的起源。传统俄国对列宁主义工程的贡献，是缺乏足够强大的社会和文化抗体来抵抗它；换句话说，她的贡献远更多是消极的而非积极的。这就是为什么世界上第一个社会主义社会，出现在据称最不具备诞生它的条件的欧洲国家。当时社会主义观念遍及欧洲，但只有在俄国，存在一个社会真空，使意识形态政治家得以不受阻碍地把这一观念付诸行动。
en: It is the inveterate weakness of Russian civil society that furnishes the distinctively Russian component to the Communist amalgam, The totalitarian nature of Communism is not to be explained as the prolongation of traditional Russian authoritarianism or Oriental despotism; nor is the collectivist nature of Soviet society to be construed as the continuation of traditional Russian communal and servile social relations. It is difficult to find any such agencies of transmission from the old to the new Russia in the actual policies pursued by the Bolsheviks after 1917, but it is very easy to find the origins of these policies in the socialist purposes of the Leninist Party. What traditional Russia contributed to the Leninist project was a lack of social and cultural antibodies sufficiently strong to resist it; in other words, her contribution was much more negative than positive. This is why the world’s first socialist society appeared in the European country that was putatively the least prepared to give birth to it. The socialist idea was everywhere in Europe at the time, but only in Russia was there a social void that permitted ideological politicians to get away with acting on it.

zh: 这种空前的社会真空，也解释了布尔什维克业绩的另一个方面。任何社会都不能作为一个未分化的平等主义大众而存在。任何社会，无论其民主精神多么强烈，都需要功能分化——社会和经济上的劳动分工——才能运作，甚至才能存在。而分化必然带来某种程度的等级、从属和不平等，大致依据技能的水平、有用性和稀缺性而定。正是这种功能和社会多元主义，构成了市民社会的基础。它也是一种正义理论的基础：社会体的每个组成部分都按其应得受到对待；这种理论同以平等为正义的现代主流观点始终处于紧张之中。
en: This unprecedented social void also explains another aspect of the Bolshevik feat. No society can exist as an undifferentiated egalitarian mass. Any society, no matter how democratic its ethos, requires functional differentiation—a social and economic division of labor—in order to operate, indeed to exist. And differentiation of necessity entails some measure of hierarchy, subordination, and inequality, approximately according to the level, usefulness, and rarity of skills. It is this functional and social pluralism that is the basis of civil society. It is also the basis of a theory of justice in which each component of the body social receives treatment according to its due, a theory that is in constant tension with the dominant modern view of justice as equality.

zh: 但在俄国，随着旧秩序一切上层梯队被截除，可以称为国家管理团体的东西消失了。于是这个无所不能的党的干部走进了这个真空。这当然是通过布尔什维克双重管理的新机制间接完成的。这样，党国至少在纸面上取代了已死的市民社会。
en: But in Russia, with the amputation of all the upper echelons of the old order, what might be called the managerial corps of the nation had disappeared. And into this void stepped the cadres of the omnicompetent Party. This was accomplished indirectly, of course, through the new mechanisms of Bolshevik dual administration. Thus, the Party-state substituted itself for the now defunct civil society, at least on paper.

zh: 结果是内战期间党员人数大幅增加。从1918年1月的约115000人，增长到1921年3月的576000人或775000人，取决于你相信哪种统计；这相当于三年内人数平均增至约原来的六倍。
因此很清楚，建设第一版苏维埃社会主义的党，不是“资本主义”下工业关系的产物，也不是1917年无产阶级热情的产物，而是内战暴力和混乱的产物。这体现在其构成上：到1921年，党员中只有少数，即41%，是工人；其余人中，28.2%是农民，30.8%是“职员及其他”，后者通常是某种小知识分子。
en: The result was an enormous increase in Party membership during the Civil War. From some 115,000 members in January 1918, the Party grew to 576,000 or 775,000 in March 1921, depending on what count one believes; this averages out to a roughly sixfold increase in three years.

So it is clear that the Party that built the first version of Soviet socialism was a product not of industrial relations under “capitalism,” nor of the proletarian ardor of 1917, but of the violence and chaos of the Civil War. And this showed in its composition: by 1921 only a minority, or 41 percent, of its members were workers; of the remainder, 28.2 percent were peasants and 30.8 percent were “employees and others,” these latter usually being some sort of petty intelligentsia.

zh: 但比党员此前的社会状况更重要的是他们入党的动机。当时追随党，意味着把一切押在它的胜利上。因此，党在很大程度上是一个由勇敢者和忠诚者组成的组织：它包括理想主义者和狂热者、向

复仇的寻求者，也包括机会主义者和暴徒。但它也是一个向上流动者的组织，是旧秩序中的工会代表和军士们的组织；对他们来说，为革命服务既是事业也是职业，未来的米哈伊尔·图哈切夫斯基元帅和谢苗·布琼尼元帅等人物就是这种品质的典型。此外，由于时局混乱、生存艰难，党也是非意识形态幸存者有利可图的避风港，1921年领导层把其中约二十万人开除出党。而由于党当时的主要事务是战争，它也是那些喜欢打仗或干脆喜欢抢劫者的家，例如游击队长恰巴耶夫，或伊萨克·巴别尔《红色骑兵军》的主人公们。
en: But what is more important than members’ previous social condition is their motivation for joining. Adhering to the Party at this time meant risking everything on its victory. Thus the Party was in significant measure an organization of the bold and the committed: it included idealists and zealots, seekers after vengeance on the

, and opportunists and thugs. But it was also an organization of the upwardly mobile, of the shop stewards and noncoms of the old order for whom service to the Revolution was both a cause and a career, qualities epitomized by such figures as the future Marshals Mikhail Tukhachevskii and Semën Budennyi. In addition, since the times were chaotic and survival difficult, the Party was a profitable berth for nonideological survivors, of whom the leadership expelled some two hundred thousand in 1921. And since the chief business of the Party at the time was war, it was also home for those who liked to fight or simply to plunder, such as the partisan leader Chapaev, or the protagonists of Isaak Babel’s

zh: 但最重要的是，党是一个从革命前阶级结构的社会原材料中创造新型人类的工具。因为当工人和农民入党时，他们获得了一种新的社会身份。他们成为一个特殊品种：共产党人、党人、充满一种不容效忠任何竞争权威的精神的战士。这些新人最典型的例子之一就是尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫：他1894年出生于库尔斯克省一个农民家庭，16岁成为工人，20岁参加红军，此后不久入党。事实上，此后二十年苏联几乎所有关键领导人，以及1930年代所有社会主义的主要建设者，都是在内战期间作为政委开始其政治生涯的。从斯大林本人开始，这份名单确实令人震惊：维亚切斯拉夫·莫洛托夫、拉扎尔·卡冈诺维奇、克利缅特·伏罗希洛夫、谢尔盖·基洛夫、瓦列里安·古比雪夫、谢尔戈·奥尔忠尼启则和安德烈·日丹诺夫。
en: But above all, the Party was a vehicle for the creation of a human being of a new type out of the social raw material of the prerevolutionary class structure. For when workers and peasants entered the Party, they acquired a new social identity. They became a special breed: Communists, Party Men, fighters imbued with a spirit that brooked allegiance to no rival authority. And here one of the most typical examples of these new men is Nikita Khrushchev, who was born in 1894 a peasant in Kursk province, became a worker at age 16, joined the Red Army when he was 20, and entered the Party soon thereafter. In fact, almost all the key leaders of the Soviet Union during the next two decades, and all the master-builders of socialism in the 1930s, cut their political teeth as commissars during the Civil War. Beginning with Stalin himself, the roster is indeed stunning: Viacheslav Molotov, Lazar Kaganovich, Klementii Voroshilov, Sergei Kirov, Valerian Kuibyshev, Sergo Ordzhonikidze, and Andrei Zhdanov.

zh: 最后，这些年的党既是一所高度英雄主义的学校，也是一所暴力统治的学校；它塑造了真正布尔什维克的形象：一个强悍、果断的战士，身穿皮夹克，胯边挂着“毛瑟同志”。因为俄国内战是这个见识过太多暴行的世纪中最残酷的插曲之一。十月之前已有三年半的世界大战，战时共产主义又加上三年半。第一次世界大战对居民的残暴化，使这个国家为内战的残暴做好了准备，而内战的残暴又进一步使居民残暴化。正如社会革命党人维克托·切尔诺夫所说，战争“抹去了人的生命——自己的和他人的——的价值。它使人变得冷酷，不在乎千百万人死亡。流血和夺走生命的权利不再是一个悲剧性问题。这就是掌权的新一代虐待狂。”
en: Finally, the Party of these years was a school of high heroism as well as of rule by violence; it produced the image of the true Bolshevik as a tough, decisive warrior with a leather jacket and “Comrade Mauser” on his hip. For the Russian Civil War was one of the most brutal episodes in a century that has known only too many. To three and one-half years of world war before October, War Communism added still another three and one-half. The brutalization of the population by the First World War prepared the country for the brutality of the Civil War, and the brutality of the Civil War then brutalized the population further still. As the SR Victor Chernov put it, war “wiped out the value of human life—both of one’s own and of others. It hardened people not to care about the death of millions. The right to spill blood and take away life ceased to be a tragic problem. Here was the new breed of sadists in power.”

zh: 的确，内战期间约有1500万人死亡，其中一些死于实际冲突本身，更多人死于流行病和饥荒。但疾病和饥荒绝非偶然因素；两者在很大程度上都是由战争破坏造成的——更西边的情况也是如此，1919年全球流感大流行夺走的生命几乎是第一次世界大战本身死亡的1000万人的两倍。但在内战期间，仅俄国就达到了地球其余地区总数的一半。除了国家的这些人口损失，还必须加上约150万旧上层阶级的移民。这些流亡者大多不是“白卫分子”，而是知识分子，他们的技能正是战后重建所严重缺乏的。
en: Indeed, around 15 million people perished during the Civil War, some of them from the actual conflict itself, even more from epidemic and famine. But disease and famine were hardly adventitious factors; both were in large measure caused by the destruction of war—as was the case also farther west, where the worldwide influenza epidemic of 1919 carried off almost: twice as many victims as the 10 million killed in the First World War itself. But during its Civil War, Russia alone reached half the figure for the rest of the planet. And to these human losses for the country must be added an emigration of around 1.5 million of the old upper classes. For the most part, these émigrés were not “White Guardists” but intelligentsia whose skills were cruelly lacking for the postwar reconstruction.

zh: 面对如此规模的灾难，把“无产阶级”对“资产阶级”的阶级胜利当作俄国革命的核心，或声称革命是工业社会“极化”的产物，是荒谬的。这些近乎文雅的马克思主义范畴，歪曲了这些年里那场党勉强控制住的、规模巨大的混乱。
en: In the light of a calamity on this scale, it is farcical to make the class triumph of the “proletariat” over the “bourgeoisie” the centerpiece of the Russian Revolution, or to claim that the Revolution was the product of the “polarization” of industrial society. These almost genteel Marxist categories denature the titanic descent into chaos, barely mastered by the Party, that characterized these years.

zh: 实际发生的事情，最好用俄国早期历史中的一个术语来描述：
。它通常译为“大动乱时期”，尤其用来指1605年至1613年间莫斯科沙皇国的崩溃和近乎消失。在那段时期，专制君主制崩溃；由世袭大贵族、服役贵族和农奴化农民组成的莫斯科社会结构几乎解体；无政府的哥萨克以及外国势力介入，瓜分了国家残存的部分。经过必要的调整，1917年至1921年间发生的是类似的政治和社会内爆，但结果截然不同：不是像1613年那样恢复
之前的秩序，而是一种全新类型秩序的胜利——意识形态统治的党治政权。
en: What did in fact occur is best described by a term from earlier Russian history,

. Usually translated as the “Time of Troubles,” this term was used in particular to designate the breakdown and near disappearance of the Tsardom of Muscovy between 1605 and 1613. During that period the autocratic monarchy collapsed; the Muscovite social structure, composed of hereditary boyars, the service gentry, and the enserfed peasantry, almost dissolved; and an anarchic Cossackry as well as foreign powers intervened to appropriate what was left of the country. Mutatis mutandis, what occurred between 1917 and 1921 was a similar political and social implosion, but one with a radically different outcome: not a restoration of the order that existed before the
, as in 1613, but the triumph of an absolutely new type of order—an ideocratic partocracy.

zh: “党治”（partocracy）是阿卜杜拉赫曼·阿夫托尔汉诺夫创造的术语，贴切地刻画了新的苏维埃政权，因为全部生活都服从于全能政党的政治命令。
但苏维埃政权也是一种“意识形态统治”（ideocracy），借用尼古拉·别尔嘉耶夫用来指世俗神权政治的术语。
在传统神权政治中，上帝并不直接统治，而是通过他的祭司统治；在苏维埃俄国这个世俗的意识形态统治中，社会主义观念间接地通过其“先锋队党”统治，在无产阶级专政中实行的实际上是机关专政。工人和农民不会创造意识形态统治的党治政权；意识形态政治家才会。
en: “Partocracy,” a term coined by Abdurakhman Avtorkhanov, aptly characterizes the new Soviet regime because all of life was subordinated to the political imperatives of the omnicompetent Party.
But the Soviet regime was also an “ideocracy,” to use Nicholas Berdiaev’s term for a secular theocracy.

In a traditional theocracy, God rules not directly but through His priests; in the secular ideocracy that was Soviet Russia, the Idea of Socialism ruled indirectly, through its “vanguard Party,” in a dictatorship of the proletariat that was in fact a dictatorship of the apparat. Workers and peasants do not create ideocratic partocracies; ideological politicians do.

zh: 因此，到1917—1921年大革命
结束时，苏维埃主义所有基本制度都已建立或初具轮廓：垄断权力（或后来所称的“领导作用”）的党国；苏维埃与机关的双重管理；契卡这一无处不在的监视者；以及最后、虽然更为试探性的中央经济计划和农业集体组织。很难相信一个内部如此连贯、功能逻辑如此自洽的制度，竟会是军事紧急状态的短暂产物。而事实上，正是这个模式提供了从斯大林到
前夜的苏联发展的主线。正如苏联人在那些漫长岁月里被教导相信的，这一事实确实“绝非偶然”。
en: Thus, by the end of the great revolutionary

of 1917-1921, all the essential institutions of Sovietism had been either created or sketched in: the Party-state, with its monopoly of power (or “leading role,” as it was later called); the dual administration of the soviets and the apparat; the universal monitor of the Cheka; and, finally though more tentatively, the central economic plan and the agricultural collective. It is difficult to believe that a system of such internal coherence and functional logic should be the passing product of military emergency. And, in actual fact, it is this model that was to furnish the main line of Soviet development from Stalin to the eve of
. As Soviets throughout those long years were taught to believe, this fact was surely “no accident.”
